item.title: Real Madrid TV takes shot at Barcelona players ahead of El Clasico: ‘They are the referees’
item.description: Real Madrid TV takes shot at Barcelona players ahead of El Clasico: ‘They are the referees’ The first El Clasico of the season is just around the corner, with Real Madrid set to lock horns with Barcelona at Camp Nou on October 25. It promises to be a feisty encounter as the relationship between the two clubs have steadily deteriorated ever since the fall of the European Super League project. Days ahead of this encounter, Real Madrid have now escalated the conflict with a fresh video on RMTV. Real Madrid take shots at Barcelona Indeed, Real Madrid’s official channel has now highlighted several refereeing flaws in the club’s recent win over Real Betis, through its latest program, reports Mundo Deportivo . The animosity between Barcelona and Real Madrid continues. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The segment, which precedes the press conferences of Jose Mourinho and Ibrahima Konate, took aim at what it perceives as preferential treatment for Barça’s players when dealing with officials. “We’re on the verge of the best competition in the world, the Champions League. There’s no dirty tricks or foul play here. And I’m sure the Leipzig players aren’t going to ask the referee to review VAR like the Barça players did in Seville,” a program began. The reference was to the incident in which Pedri and Lamine Yamal protested for a handball in the build-up to Lo Celso’s goal, prompting referee De Burgos Bengoetxea to remark: “Check the handball, that’s what they’re asking me to do.” Warning ahead of the Clasico Are the odds stacked against Mourinho’s men. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) From there, the channel escalated its rhetoric, framing the upcoming Clasico as a contest stacked against Los Blancos . “Now the Barça players are the new referees and they demand VAR on demand. When our players approach the referee, they’re kept away, but the Barça players have free rein,” the program stated. The show then delivered the most provocative line of all, suggesting Madrid would be up against far more than 11 opponents at the Camp Nou. “That’s why next Sunday we’ll be facing 17 referees: those on the pitch, those in VAR, and the 11 Barcelona players ,” the show concluded. This will not go down well with Barcelona, though the Catalans are, at the moment, focused on their upcoming battle against Paris Saint-Germain, whereas Real Madrid are slated to take on RB Leipzig tomorrow night, in the UEFA Champions League.

item.title: Morgan Rogers reveals how Chelsea teammate Joao Pedro has taken his game to the next level
item.description: Joao Pedro has been Chelsea ’s standout attacking force this season, and Morgan Rogers believes the Brazilian is at the peak of his powers as he praised his in-form team-mate’s “hunger to score” for Xabi Alonso ’s side. Only Manchester City’s Erling Haaland has outscored Pedro in the Premier League so far, with eight goals to the Chelsea forward’s five in six matches. Those goals have played their part in lifting the Blues to fourth in the table during Alonso’s first campaign at the Stamford Bridge helm. England international Rogers, who joined the west London club from Aston Villa in a £117million deal this summer, said: “I think his (Pedro’s) hunger to score goals, his hunger to work for the team is massive. “Especially for me, where I play on the pitch, it really helps me loads. He always gives me an option. I can always play off him, and he can play off me, too. “He’s a massive part of us, not just scoring goals, he works so hard as well. The relentless running in the channel and working defensively as well for the team. Morgan Rogers has started well at Chelsea (Getty) “A lot of his focus is also on getting goals, being in the box. He’s worked on it in training about arriving, getting in the box and scoring goals and he’s been doing that every game since I’ve been here. “He’s on the top of his game right now and it’s really good for Chelsea that he is.” Rogers has made a bright start of his own since his British-record transfer, contributing four goals and one assist in the league. He continued: “I’m feeling really good when I go out there, feeling really confident. The players and the staff allow me to be me, which is the most important thing, and I can just play my game and focus on that. “I’ve still got improvements that I want to make in my game, but I’m happy with the start. I think the start’s the important thing and you try and get fans on your side, try and get the players on your side, which is tough. “So I’m glad that I can do that, but it’s just about moving forward with the team. It’s a long project and it’s going in the right direction.” Tottenham are the visitors to Stamford Bridge on Saturday evening. Chelsea then travel to Liverpool in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup next week.

item.title: Deion Sanders Shares Emotional Message After Ex-Heisman Finalist’s NFL Dream Takes Hit
item.description: Diego Pavia climbed from New Mexico State to Vanderbilt and finished second in the 2025 Heisman voting. Then came the NFL, and it was over before a single regular-season game. So his future went right back to being unclear. But here’s the thing about old football connections. They don’t just vanish. A weekend in Boulder put Pavia back in front of coach Deion Sanders who once offered him a scholarship. Deion Sanders Sends Diego Pavia a Public Show of Support Well, the message didn’t take long to land, and it was personal. Deion Sanders responded to Pavia’s Instagram post with, “Love ya, man! You are a real 1. God bless u.” Sanders wrote that after the former Vanderbilt quarterback thanked Colorado for its welcome. Apr 11, 2026; Boulder, CO, USA; Colorado Buffaloes head coach Deion Sanders during the spring game at Folsom Field. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images “Boulder, thank you guys, for an awesome experience. I loved the way you guys got rowdy for the ball players.” He continued, “I was super entertained myself, and I will definitely be back to support my guys! SKOO BUFFS ???? Also thank you to @deionsanders & @deionsandersjr for taking care of me this weekend and treating me like family. Love you guys forever. For you guys that didn’t get to watch, check out my YouTube channel for the lit weekend!!” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Diego Pavia (@diego10pavia) The exchange followed Pavia’s visit to Colorado’s game against Utah on October 17. He said he went to support Sanders after telling viewers on a livestream, “I do wish I could play for Coach Prime.” And Pavia added that none of it happens without Sanders’ earlier offer. So what was that offer, exactly? It goes back to Sanders’ time at Jackson State. Pavia said Sanders was honest with him that he’d sit behind Sanders’ son, Shedeur. So Pavia chose New Mexico State first, then transferred to Vanderbilt. Diego Pavia’s NFL Future Remains Unsettled After Ravens Waiver Now, the timing of all this matters because Pavia’s college résumé did not earn him a draft selection. He threw for 3,539 yards and 29 touchdowns at Vanderbilt in 2025, added 862 rushing yards and 10 scores, and finished second in Heisman voting to Fernando Mendoza. Vanderbilt quarterback Diego Pavia, left, chats with freshman quarterback Jared Curtis, right, during football pro day at Vanderbilt University in Nashville, Tenn., Friday, March 20, 2026. After all that, the Baltimore Ravens signed Pavia as an undrafted free agent in April and gave him a three-year, $3.1 million contract. Then came July 23. They waived him to clear a roster spot for veteran offensive lineman Ethan Pocic. Just like that, Pavia had no team. Sanders had already gone public with encouragement after the release, posting, “I BELIEVE IN YOU, MY MAN!” That message and the new Instagram reply show continued personal support, but neither confirms a coaching role or a path back onto a roster. Deion Sanders a.k.a. Coach Rime of the Colorado B

item.title: Nick Sirianni Gets Testy in Heated Presser Over Jalen Hurts Fly Back Decision After Blood Clot Diagnosis
item.description: Nick Sirianni faced a tough room on Monday after the Philadelphia Eagles fell 25-14 to the Carolina Panthers, dropping them to 2-4. The coach expected questions about a slumping team. Instead, one topic dominated the session, and it centered on quarterback Jalen Hurts . What Sirianni said, and how he said it, quickly became the story, and it left fresh questions hanging over the organization. Nick Sirianni Clashes with Reporter over Jalen Hurts Flight Decision The exchange came during Sirianni’s Monday press conference, hours after the Eagles and Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, released a joint statement. It confirmed that Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning clots in both lungs. League sources told CBS Philadelphia he is expected to miss the rest of the season. The questions grew sharper because of the timeline. Hurts was cleated against the Rams on Oct. 4 and sought treatment on Oct. 8. A London ultrasound before the Jaguars game showed a superficial clot, and doctors cleared him to play. Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) drops back to pass during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images PennLive reported that they also told him not to sleep before the game as a precaution. Hurts played in the 19-17 loss, then flew home with the team. Reporters pressed Sirianni on both decisions. Asked why Hurts was allowed to fly home from London with a blood clot, the coach replied: “Again, I’m not a medical expert, same type same deal there,” Sirianni said . “We get medical information from our guys, and we always put the players health first and foremost in every situation.” Earlier, when asked if the Eagles could have done anything differently, Sirianni said, “I have full trust and full faith in them,” about the medical staff. He also repeated that the team had issued multiple statements. #Eagles HC Nick Sirianni got into a back-and-forth with a reporter over why Jalen Hurts was allowed to fly back from London after being diagnosed with a blood clot: https://t.co/QqlEpCXhAc — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 19, 2026 Sirianni declined to name who on the medical staff joined the pregame talks about Hurts’ availability, and he kept the quarterback’s reaction private. Even before the diagnosis became public, one doctor had raised an alarming possibility about where this was heading Doctor Flagged Season-Ending Risk for Jalen Hurts Before Eagles Update Two days earlier, sports medicine specialist Dr. Brian Sutterer weighed in after the team placed Hurts on injured reserve. Sutterer warned online, “don’t be surprised when the next news is that his season is over.” He explained that a superficial clot can extend into a deep vein clot, which can lead to a pulmonary embolism. The Eagles (2-4) have lost four straight and now host the Dallas Cowboys (2-4) for Monday Night Football on Oct. 26. Tanner McKee is expected to keep leading the offense, while Sirianni will likely face more questions about Hurts. item.title: ‘Perhaps one of the best pressing systems I’ve ever seen’ – Club Brugge manager Ivan Leko on RC Lens ‘very good’ team
item.description: ‘Perhaps one of the best pressing systems I’ve ever seen’ – Club Brugge manager Ivan Leko on RC Lens ‘very good’ team A week after their resounding victory away at Inter Milan (3-4), Club Brugge are set to face a challenge of a completely different calibre this Wednesday, as they host RC Lens on Matchday 3 of the Champions League group stage. Having lost 0-2 at home to Sporting CP eight days ago, Les Sang et Or – currently 34th out of 36 in the overall standings – head to the Jan Breydelstadion as underdogs. However, Brugge manager Ivan Leko refuses to underestimate his opponents. Whilst he acknowledges that the names of the Lens players are obviously not as “appealing” as those found “at Inter, Liverpool, Barça or Arsenal” , the Croatian manager remains wary of the northerners. “When you start watching the matches – four or five of them – under a new manager, and you take a look at how the team has performed in Ligue 1 over the last five or six years, they’re a very strong opponent,” Leko pointed out. “They’re better than I expected. They might not have any world-class players, but they’re a very good side.” A team which, in his view, displays “perhaps one of the best pressing games I’ve seen. A team that’s strong in one-on-one situations and runs a lot.” A potential pitfall in the face of which Leko expects his team to show “humility” , whilst also asking them to “know where we stand and who we are” . GFFN | Léo Aschi

item.title: Injury means big break comes at last for Chelsea academy starlet who could face Liverpool
item.description: Injury means big break comes at last for Chelsea academy starlet who could face Liverpool For now, Mike Penders is Chelsea’s new number one. That means there’s a goalkeeper on the bench for the Blues. If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. While Chelsea got an important win on Saturday against Everton, there was bad news too. Goalkeeper Emi Martinez had a horrific collision with an attacker and ended up having surgery on a broken jaw. That meant young Mike Penders game into the game, and will now keep his place for the foreseeable future, starting on Saturday against Tottenham. Dom Smith has written a piece for the Evening Standard looking at Penders and what fans can expect from the 21 year old. Penders and TSL move up the chain Mike Penders makes Premier League debut. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) As Penders steps up from number two to number one, so Teddy Sharman-Lowe goes from third choice to second. The academy keeper has had some good loan spells in the lower leagues, and looks set to get a Championship or European move after this season. The question is whether TSL will play games like the Liverpool match in the EFL Cup next week. That would have been Penders’ match if Martinez was still fit – does it now go to the next man up, or does Alonso decide to keep the Belgian in there to accelerate the development of his relationship with the defence ahead of him? We suspect it will be the latter. In other news… Xabi Alonso confirmed on Saturday that Pep Chavarria would have tests on an injury he picked up in training before the game against Everton. Former England defender Stuart Pearce was among the pundits impressed by Pender’s showing on Saturday.

item.title: Carrick navigating five first-team injury woes on eve of Como clash as ‘crisis’ now in full swing
item.description: Carrick navigating five first-team injury woes on eve of Como clash as ‘crisis’ now in full swing Michael Carrick is working with a severely depleted squad ahead of Manchester United’s clash with Como tomorrow. The players took part in an open training session at Carrington today before flying to Italy, and as many as five senior players were absent. Who’s missing for United? (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) As per BBC Sport’s Simon Stone , Ayden Heaven, Lisandro Martinez, Luke Shaw, Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford were not involved, while Leny Yoro trained separately , as his suspension following last week’s red card means he is ruled out anyway. Manchester Evening News journalist Steven Railston subsequently added that Carrick is facing a ‘defensive crisis’ at potentially the worst possible time, given he is in a place where wins are imperative. Harry Maguire, Diogo Dalot, Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt are poised to be the only senior defenders available, with the latter awaiting his first appearance since November 2025. Carrick facing an uphill battle to turn around United’s form (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Rashford is said to have been nursing a hip problem since the World Cup, hence choosing to withdraw from the England squad over the international break. Meanwhile, Martinez was hooked at the interval of Sunday’s draw with Leeds United after feeling some discomfort in his thigh. item.title: What time is Rutgers football vs. Northwestern? TV, prediction for Week 8
item.description: It’s been 17 years since Rutgers football beat a ranked opponent. The Scarlet Knights ’ next chance to end that streak will be on Saturday, Oct. 24 when they play Northwestern at the new Ryan Field in Evanston, Illinois. Rutgers, whose last ranked win came on Nov. 12, 2009 when it beat No. 23 South Florida, is coming off a 37-30 win over Maryland. Northwestern, which has been on a consistent climb under David Braun, is coming off a 24-21 win over Michigan State. The Scarlet Knights have already played two ranked teams this season – USC and Indiana – but lost to both (they did push the Trojans in a seven-point win). Rutgers is 4-2 all time against Northwestern. The keys for the Scarlet Knights in this game will be to avoid turnovers, get the ball into the hands of KJ Duff and play consistently on defense for all four quarters, something Rutgers hasn’t done well this season. Northwestern has become one of the better middle-tier teams in the Big Ten. The Scarlet Knights will need a clean performance if they’re going to pick up a second-straight road victory. Rutgers football schedule: Scarlet Knights' next game Rutgers plays Northwestern on Saturday, Oct. 24 at Ryan Field in their Week 8 game. What time is Rutgers vs. Northwestern? Kickoff is scheduled for Noon ET. What channel is Rutgers vs. Northwestern? The game will be streamed on Peacock. WATCH Rutgers vs. Northwestern on Peacock Rutgers vs. Northwestern spread Rutgers is a 16.5-point underdog, according to Vegas Insider. Rutgers vs. Northwestern prediction Northwestern has been one of the surprise teams in the Big Ten last year, steadily improving under David Braun. The Wildcats pushed Indiana, beat Penn State and just beat Michigan State (although that win was by just three points and the Wildcats were far from perfect in a mistake-filled performance). They're averaging 424.5 yards per game while giving up 368.0 per contest. Quarterback Aidan Chiles is a much-improved player from the one he was at Michigan State. He's completing 70.5 percent of his passes and has thrown for 1,398 yards and nine touchdowns. Overall right now, Northwestern is just a better team than Rutgers is. While the Scarlet Knights have shown improvement since the start of the season, going on the road and beating a ranked team is a tall order for where they are right now. Score prediction: Northwestern 31, Rutgers 20 Rutgers vs. Northwestern tickets Buy tickets for Rutgers vs. Northwestern on StubHub. Both clubs earned the No. 1 seed in their respective leagues and proved why they were the best in baseball by reaching the final stage. The Brewers enter the World Series coming off an emphatic beatdown of the two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers . Milwaukee not only knocked off the heavy favorites to win the championship, but did so in a four-game sweep, not giving L.A. any breathing room for a comeback. On the other side of the bracket, the Rays punched their ticket to the World Series with a Game 6 win over the Cleveland Guardians . After allowing seven runs in a Game 1 loss, the Tampa Bay pitching staff held the Guardians to just 10 runs in five games. Between budding young talent like Jackson Chourio, Jacob Misiorowski and Junior Caminero, to elder statesmen such as Christian Yelich and Yandy Diaz, the 2026 World Series is sure to deliver theatrics. Or will the Brewers prove they are the best team in baseball and cap off a franchise-altering season with rings? The Sporting News hands out its expert predictions for the 2026 World Series. item.content:encoded: World Series predictions 2026: Sporting News projects Brewers vs. Rays championship series originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A first-time World Series champion will be crowned in 2026. The end of October is approaching, and after a grueling few weeks, only two clubs remain in the MLB playoff bracket: the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays . Both clubs earned the No. 1 seed in their respective leagues and proved why they were the best in baseball by reaching the final stage. The Brewers enter the World Series coming off an emphatic beatdown of the two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers . Milwaukee not only knocked off the heavy favorites to win the championship, but did so in a four-game sweep, not giving L.A. any breathing room for a comeback. On the other side of the bracket, the Rays punched their ticket to the World Series with a Game 6 win over the Cleveland Guardians . After allowing seven runs in a Game 1 loss, the Tampa Bay pitching staff held the Guardians to just 10 runs in five games. Between budding young talent like Jackson Chourio, Jacob Misiorowski and Junior Caminero, to elder statesmen such as Christian Yelich and Yandy Diaz, the 2026 World Series is sure to deliver theatrics. Will the Rays deliver what they could not in 2021 and bring a World Series title to Tampa Bay? Or will the Brewers prove they are the best team in baseball and cap off a franchise-altering season with rings? The Sporting News hands out its expert predictions for the 2026 World Series. MORE: Complete start times, schedule for 2026 World Series World Series predictions 2026 Imagn Images Dan Treacy, Senior Content Producer World Series winner prediction: Brewers over Rays World Series MVP prediction: Jackson Chourio, Brewers This is a fairly unprecedented matchup with two teams chasing their first championship. That makes predicting the series difficult, but it's hard to side against the team that has proven all season long to be the best in baseball in spite of their payroll. The Brewers are facing a Rays team that excels at run prevention, but it speaks volumes that Milwaukee wasn't intimidated in the slightest by a Dodgers rotation of Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. If Milwaukee can grind out at-bats against that group, the lineup can surely handle a deep Rays staff. The difference between these two teams is the depth of the Brewers' offense. Both have excellent pitching staffs; the Rays have more starters, but the Brewers have the better bullpen. The top of Tampa Bay's lineup is intimidating - Junior Caminero heating up in the clinching game of the ALCS should grab the Brewers' attention - but the rest of the lineup is much weaker. The Rays haven't hit for much power in this postseason, and that doesn't bode well as they face an even better staff. The Brewers, on the other hand, have a slew of options for just about every situation. Just about every position player at Pat Murphy's disposal is extremely useful in some way, and so many of Milwaukee's bats have proven they can come through in big spots. From Jackson Chourio to William Contreras, their best hitters simply seem built for these moments. Whether the Rays' offense will be able to answer those moments is a legitimate question. One prediction that we know will come true: someone is going to win the World Series for the first time. The Brewers are better positioned to finish the job. MORE: Where Rays, Brewers rank among longest World Series droughts Jerome Miron-USA TODAY Sports Bryan Murphy, Deputy News Editor World Series winner : Rays over Brewers World Series MVP : Yandy Diaz, Rays Before the playoffs, I said that it would be the Rays emerging victorious in 2026 — and that prediction hasn't been swayed. Tampa Bay plays about as clean of a game of baseball as you'll find. Offensively, they get guys on base, they put the ball in play and they don't run into outs. It's not pretty, but it's effective. Their starting pitching is stellar and backed by breakout closer Bryan Baker, the bullpen has been nails. With that said, the Brewers play an almost identical style. Their offense provides a little more juice than the Rays, but Tampa Bay has the upper hand on starting pitching. Kevin Cash's team will rely once again on their pitching to shut down some dangerous Milwaukee bats in Jackson Chourio, Brice Turang and more. For MVP, the flashy pick would be Junior Caminero, but I'm going to go with Yandy Diaz. He's been a consistent force in the leadoff spot for years for the Rays, and he's been their best hitter this October, batting .310 with two home runs and six RBIs these playoffs. Expect the 35-year-old to make some more noise in the World Series. MORE: How Rays landed Junior Caminero in deal with Guardians Daniel Chavkin, Content Producer World Series winner : Brewers over Rays World Series MVP : Jackson Chourio, Brewers I picked Brewers over Rays before the playoffs began, so I'm sticking with Milwaukee to take home its first World Series title. The Brewers will benefit from their NLCS sweep, as their bullpen should be fresh for the World Series and allow Pat Murphy to manage without worrying about overworking his group. Additionally, Milwaukee's offense will give the Rays more of a challenge than the Yankees or Guardians did, as the unit dispatched a star-studded Dodgers rotation in four games. Tampa Bay has more reliable starting pitchers, which could be crucial if the series goes long, but the Brewers' deeper bullpen and timely hitting will be too much for the Rays to overcome. Daniel Mader, Content Producer World Series winner: Brewers over Rays World Series MVP: Brice Turang, Brewers If you like small ball, this is your World Series. I expect we’re in for at least six games of Brewers vs. Rays — both teams have the pitching, depth, and relentless offensive approach to win the series. They’ll push each other to the limit. In the end, though, I think Milwaukee having the best pitcher in the series, Jacob Misiorowski, several trusted bullpen arms and a collection of bats with momentum from sweeping the Dodgers will put Pat Murphy’s team over the top. I think we’re in for a reminder why Brice Turang has become one of the best second basemen in baseball. He’s homered off both Nick Martinez and Drew Rasmussen before, as have Christian Yelich and William Contreras. But I’ll take Turang to claim World Series MVP, powering the Brewers to their first championship. MORE: Inside Jacob Misiorowki's insane velocity Andrew Gitto, Editorial Intern World Series winner: Brewers over Rays World Series MVP: Jake Bauers, Brewers No need to rub your eyes, Milwaukee fans; the Brewers are an incredibly good side. Along with boasting the best batting average (.258) and second-most runs (832) during the regular season, their combination of batting, starting pitchers, and bullpen is just too good for any team to overcome. Not many teams in MLB history can say they’ve swept the LA Dodgers in the postseason and that’s an ode to Pat Murphy’s crew. Milwaukee has too many advantages, which is why I’m picking them to win their first-ever World Series. Milwaukee’s first baseman Jake Bauers was an integral part of orchestrating their Game 4 comeback against the Dodgers, and he’s coming off an NLCS that saw him get a hit in every game. He’s playing phenomenal baseball coming into the World Series, and that good form should continue. He’s batting .269 (7-for-26) with six RBIs (5th among postseason batters), and his bat has been red-hot. item.title: Man Utd facing defensive shortage ahead of Como clash
item.description: Man Utd facing defensive shortage ahead of Como clash Manchester United were without a host of first-team players in training ahead of their Champions League trip to Como. Ayden Heaven, Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martinez, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Sesko were all absent from Tuesday morning’s session at Carrington. Patrick Dorgu and Manuel Ugarte also remain out with longer term issues. Martinez was withdrawn at half-time during Sunday’s 1-1 draw with Leeds United , with Noussair Mazraoui replacing him. Heaven missed the game at Elland Road through illness, having started at left-back against Atletico Madrid. Shaw and Mainoo have now missed United’s last two matches, while Rashford is continuing to manage an injury issue. There was more positive news on Matthijs de Ligt, who has returned to the group following surgery on a back problem, although he is yet to feature since his recovery. Leny Yoro will also miss the Como game through suspension. Youngsters Dan Armer and Jaydan Kamason were both involved in training as Michael Carrick’s side prepared to travel to Italy for their third Champions League fixture of the season.

item.title: The Moments that Made the 2026 Red Sox: One lucky night in August was the fork in the road
item.description: Boston, MA - August 22: Boston Red Sox right fielder Wilyer Abreu is mobbed after hitting a walk-off single. The Boston Red Sox played the San Francisco Giants at Fenway Park on August 22, 2026. (Photo by Barry Chin/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images I didn’t know it when I was sitting in the bleachers at Fenway during that Saturday night in August, but the Red Sox’s wild 3-2 walk-off victory against the Giants on August 22 might’ve been the fork in the road for the 2026 season. Maybe it’s arbitrary to say that one game out of 162 was the moment where this iteration of the club crossed the Rubicon, where the magic of the preceding summer weeks continued but the base line for what was to come was laid out without us even knowing it at the time. But with the benefit of hindsight, I think that’s what game 129 was for us. The TL;DR recap of the game: Patrick Sandoval wasn’t good enough on the bump as Boston’s starter, but he was somehow able to limit the damage to just two runs. After sleepwalking for most of the game, the Red Sox bats eventually woke up and clawed back to tie the game in the ninth. With the bases then loaded, Wilyer Abreu hit a hard grounder to first. The throw home took the Giants’ catcher off the plate, Eli White slid in head first, and the Sox stormed the field in jubilation. The review from the umps then proceeded to go on for what felt like an hour, but the call—and in turn Boston’s victory—was confirmed. What a night to be at the ballpark, man. I remember my head hurting from screaming so much following the walk-off, but I didn’t care. What a win in a summer filled with excellent wins. It’s been said before many-a-times at this point, but it’s worth repeating: I’m glad the Sox gave us our summer back after a horrid spring, even if they couldn’t give us much of a fall. That’s a win I’ll remember for a while. I’ll especially remember it thanks to the bizarre ending as well. That review process, where we weren’t sure how the decision was going to pan out (or if it ever was going to be made, my goodness it took forever) was unlike something I had seen in person at Fenway. The walk-off celebration, followed by the prolonged review, followed by another walk-off celebration once the call was confirmed; that’s just a funny (well, at least for us Sox fans that night) and unique order of events. Just when you think you’ve seen everything at a baseball game… And yet, that Saturday night in August ended up being one of the last times we were truly galvanized by the 2026 Boston Red Sox, no? That win against San Francisco was the second victory en route to a sweep, and the Sox then immediately took the first two games in Miami, but the following weekend was where we dropped three games out of four in New York towards the end of August. item.content:encoded: Boston, MA - August 22: Boston Red Sox right fielder Wilyer Abreu is mobbed after hitting a walk-off single. The Boston Red Sox played the San Francisco Giants at Fenway Park on August 22, 2026. (Photo by Barry Chin/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images I didn’t know it when I was sitting in the bleachers at Fenway during that Saturday night in August, but the Red Sox’s wild 3-2 walk-off victory against the Giants on August 22 might’ve been the fork in the road for the 2026 season. Maybe it’s arbitrary to say that one game out of 162 was the moment where this iteration of the club crossed the Rubicon, where the magic of the preceding summer weeks continued but the base line for what was to come was laid out without us even knowing it at the time. But with the benefit of hindsight, I think that’s what game 129 was for us. The TL;DR recap of the game: Patrick Sandoval wasn’t good enough on the bump as Boston’s starter, but he was somehow able to limit the damage to just two runs. I remember my head hurting from screaming so much following the walk-off, but I didn’t care. What a win in a summer filled with excellent wins. It’s been said before many-a-times at this point, but it’s worth repeating: I’m glad the Sox gave us our summer back after a horrid spring, even if they couldn’t give us much of a fall. That’s a win I’ll remember for a while. I’ll especially remember it thanks to the bizarre ending as well. That review process, where we weren’t sure how the decision was going to pan out (or if it ever was going to be made, my goodness it took forever) was unlike something I had seen in person at Fenway. The walk-off celebration, followed by the prolonged review, followed by another walk-off celebration once the call was confirmed; that’s just a funny (well, at least for us Sox fans that night) and unique order of events. Just when you think you’ve seen everything at a baseball game… And yet, that Saturday night in August ended up being one of the last times we were truly galvanized by the 2026 Boston Red Sox, no? That win against San Francisco was the second victory en route to a sweep, and the Sox then immediately took the first two games in Miami, but the following weekend was where we dropped three games out of four in New York towards the end of August. After the walk-off to get the team up to 11 games over .500, the Sox finished the regular season on a 17-16 run (and we just established that three of those wins game before the Yankees series, so things really ended on a whimper). It was the latest chapter of the magical run that was Summer 2K26 at Fenway, but it was one of the first examples of what would eventually be one of the major factors as to why there was no Fall 2K26 at Fenway: the offensive struggles. As our fearless leader Dan mentioned in his game summary for the win, Boston get just one guy into scoring position prior to the 8th inning. The lack of output at the dish wasn’t the only reason we got bounced from the playoffs a few weeks ago, but I think it was obviously the biggest reason. The woes with the bats did not come out of nowhere; that was a concerning trend for basically all of September. Pitching was able to keep the boys in a lot of games—much like it did during this game—but that alone would not be enough in the end. I guess you could make the argument that this win sort of encapsulated the Red Sox’s entire post-Colorado-road-trip story. If you had to pick one game to be the microcosm of this club’s second half, I’d say this was the one. It featured the magic that got them back into the hunt and the Achilles heel that knocked them right back out of it. The walk-off on August 22 was sensational, but summer effectively ended once Eli White slid across the plate. We just didn’t know it at the time.

item.title: Iga Swiatek Withdraws from Ningbo, Won’t Qualify for WTA Finals
item.description: Tennis - U.S. Open - Flushing Meadows, New York, United States - September 7, 2026 Poland's Iga Swiatek in action during her round of 16 match against China's Qinwen Zheng REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Steen Kirby Six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek has withdrawn from the Ningbo Open due to an ongoing left thigh injury, effectively ending her chances of qualifying directly for the 2026 WTA Finals . The Polish star confirmed the decision in a statement released by tournament organizers on Tuesday. “After careful consideration, I’ve decided to withdraw from the tournament. I’ve been experiencing an ongoing problem with my left thigh over the past weeks and I feel that giving myself the time to rest and recover is the right decision,” Swiatek said. The injury first became apparent during her Wuhan Open semifinal loss to compatriot Maja Chwalinska last weekend. Swiatek required a medical timeout, played with her left thigh bandaged, and struggled with movement as she fell in straight sets. She had ignored earlier advice from her physiotherapist to retire from that match. This is the first year since 2019 that Swiatek will not qualify for the season-ending championships as one of the top eight players in the Race. She had earned a place in 2020, though the event was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Her only remaining route into the Indian Wells field is now as an alternate. Swiatek entered the final stretch of the season competing with Karolina Muchova and Marta Kostyuk for the last available spot. Muchova currently holds the eighth position in the Race standings. With Ningbo off the table and the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo still to come, the former world No. 1 can no longer close the gap sufficiently even with a title run in Japan. Sep 3, 2025; Flushing, NY, USA; Iga Swiatek (POL) hits a forehand against Amanda Anisimova (USA) (not pictured) on day eleven of the 2025 US Open tennis championships at USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images The Last Word The withdrawal marks a difficult close to a challenging 2026 campaign for the 25-year-old, who has struggled to recapture the dominance of previous seasons. Fans and the tennis community have wished her a swift recovery as she prioritises her long-term fitness. Swiatek’s absence from Ningbo reshapes the final qualification picture and leaves the door open for others in the race for the season’s last major stage. Main Photo Credit: REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz

With Ningbo off the table and the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo still to come, the former world No. 1 can no longer close the gap sufficiently even with a title run in Japan. Sep 3, 2025; Flushing, NY, USA; Iga Swiatek (POL) hits a forehand against Amanda Anisimova (USA) (not pictured) on day eleven of the 2025 US Open tennis championships at USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images The Last Word The withdrawal marks a difficult close to a challenging 2026 campaign for the 25-year-old, who has struggled to recapture the dominance of previous seasons. Fans and the tennis community have wished her a swift recovery as she prioritises her long-term fitness. Swiatek’s absence from Ningbo reshapes the final qualification picture and leaves the door open for others in the race for the season’s last major stage. Main Photo Credit: REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz

item.title: NFC South Week 6 Review: There’s finally a team over .500
item.description: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Jalen Ramsey #5 of the Pittsburgh Steelers sacks Jalon Daniels #10 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images As it often does, the division split wins and losses this week, with the Saints and Panthers coming out on top. The Buccaneers failed to build on last week’s win, and the Falcons are in the midst of their 2nd losing streak of the season. Here’s the Week 6 NFC South Review: Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-5) Week 6 Result: Buccaneers 19 – Steelers 26 Week 7 Opponent: Carolina Panthers Jalon Daniels is fun to watch, mainly because he’s not playing for my team. The UDFA is doing his best, but the limitations are clear, and as Falcons fans can attest, Zac Robinson won’t do much to alleviate them. The Buccaneers had a 13-point lead going into the 4th quarter and squandered it, giving up 16 points and pushing the contest to overtime. Being careless with the football and asking a UDFA to throw the ball 43 times proved to be their undoing. There’s a chance Baker Mayfield could return soon , but it’s unlikely he’ll mask this team’s issues. Next week they take on the division leaders in Charlotte. JALEN RAMSEY CALLS GAME! STEELERS WIN 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/MYHqLZM0jO — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 Carolina Panthers (3-2) Week 6 Result: Panthers 25 – Eagles 14 Week 7 Opponent: Tampa Bay Buccaneers After a bye week they desperately needed, the Panthers took care of business against a decimated Eagles . Carolina’s offense looks like a well-oiled machine right now. They sit atop the division as the only team in the South above .500. Some might call them “schedule merchants,” but you don’t get to pick the opponents you play, and as every NFL fan has learned, there’s no such thing as easy games in this league. Tyler Shough’s all-around play wasn’t that impressive, but he delivered when he absolutely had to. item.title: Michigan State basketball has 1 goal in exhibition with UConn
item.description: EAST LANSING – Of all the recent rules changes in college sports Tom Izzo has disliked, there is one he truly has embraced. Playing anyone, anywhere at any time – and not having it count against his record with Michigan State basketball . For the second straight season, Izzo and the No. 6 Spartans will face Dan Hurley and No. 5 Connecticut in an exhibition game, with tipoff set for Breslin Center on Tuesday, Oct. 20 (7 p.m., BTN+). RELATED: Couch: Jesse McCulloch could be MSU basketball's latest development story Last preseason, MSU went to Hartford, Connecticut, fell behind big and then rallied late in a 76-69 exhibition loss to UConn. But it wasn't the only time they met; Hurley’s Huskies ended the Spartans’ season with a 67-63 win in the Sweet 16 on March 27 in Washington. “Like last year, it'll be a good test for us,” Izzo said Thursday, Oct. 15. “The problem now when you're playing these big exhibition games is you have to figure out what exhibition games are really for – to see what you have, to see how your team improved, to see what guys fit with what guys, to mix up the lineups, see who's improved – and get an idea. “The great thing for me is getting an idea against a team and a coach that I know pretty well. I know Danny real well. We're both looking for the same thing – to see where our team's at.” Izzo said Hurley called him after MSU’s win over Arkansas in last year's second regular-season game to give him some critique of what he saw during the exhibition game they played. “We didn't play very well out there last year, and he called me a couple weeks later after we had beaten Arkansas or somebody really good, and said, ‘God, I was worried for you, because I thought your team was awful,’ ” Izzo said. “Only Danny could be honest like that. I would have said the same thing to him. I said, ‘We were awful, but you had something to do with it.’ But I knew we were better than what we played. “That's part of the preseason. I know Danny real well. We're both looking for the same thing – to see where our team's at.” Izzo said Hurley called him after MSU’s win over Arkansas in last year's second regular-season game to give him some critique of what he saw during the exhibition game they played. “We didn't play very well out there last year, and he called me a couple weeks later after we had beaten Arkansas or somebody really good, and said, ‘God, I was worried for you, because I thought your team was awful,’ ” Izzo said. “Only Danny could be honest like that. I would have said the same thing to him. I said, ‘We were awful, but you had something to do with it.’ But I knew we were better than what we played. “That's part of the preseason. You've got to make sure you keep it all in perspective.” JEFF SEIDEL: How a student journalist got MSU coach Tom Izzo to fill with emotion UConn, which advanced to April's national title game before losing to Michigan, opened its exhibition slate with a 72-52 win over Syracuse last Tuesday. Na'jai Hines had 17 points and eight rebounds, while Silas Demary Jr. scored 13 and Nik Khamenia 12. The Huskies will finish exhibition play against Purdue on Oct. 27. MSU, which dismantled Incarnate Word, 89-59, on Oct. 2 at Breslin, has had a bit of a break between preseason games. It is the first time Izzo has three exhibition games on the slate, taking advantage of a recently enacted rule adding another chance for teams to get in work before the games count toward standings and NCAA Tournament resumes. “We've already played one exhibition game, and we were OK,” Izzo said. “I thought our young guys really looked young the first time we put them in. Subbing by hockey lines is sometimes what I do, especially in the first exhibition game. It's not necessarily great for anybody, meaning our players – other than to get the definite opportunity to play.” Izzo said he expects to mix up his lineup more against the Huskies and potentially again Sunday, when the Spartans head to Milwaukee, to face Shaka Smart’s Marquette on Sunday (1 p.m., YouTube). MSU opens the regular season against Quinnipiac on Nov. 2. “I really respect what Shaka's done there,” Izzo said. “And I think it'll be a different test, but a good test for us before we start moving on.” Contact Chris Solari: csolari@freepress.com . item.title: Xs and Ohs! Purdue and Washington Edition
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE, INDIANA - OCTOBER 16: Antonio Harris #22 of the Purdue Boilermakers celebrates a touchdown with Boaz Stanley #50 of the Purdue Boilermakers against the Washington Huskies at Ross-Ade Stadium on October 16, 2026 in West Lafayette, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images You may have heard that the website formerly known as Twitter has been purchased and is now X, a simply horrendous name in my opinion but then again I am not a billionaire so take my suggestions with a grain of salt. You may also know that we have historically shared our favorite tweets from game day the Monday after a football game in a story known as In Tweets. Well, Twitter is gone and it ain’t comin’ back! As much as I’ll still call it Stadium Dining Court, most of you will still call it Deer Creek, and it’ll always be Burma to J. Peterman that site and app will always be Twitter to me. But for those who eat at Ford, see music at Ruoff Music Center, and visit Myanmar I decided to rename this article. This article is of course a play on words for the excellent Ellie King song Ex’s and Oh’s and the new name of Twitter. I promise it’s a great name. You’ll get used to it. The scene at Ross-Ade Stadium before @BoilerFootball ’s Friday night matchup against Washington 🚂 pic.twitter.com/IOYX1Jwtzr — Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) October 17, 2026 First play of the game and @BoilerFootball comes up with the pick 🤯 pic.twitter.com/uwaTvEkQPx — FOX College Football (@CFBONFOX) October 17, 2026 pic.twitter.com/k8mwTdviYJ — Casual Purdue (@CasualPurdue) October 17, 2026 I agree with going for it but C'mon man you need to call more aggressive and better plays than a run up the gut. — Mitten Boilermaker (@Purduefan19) October 17, 2026 Great night for some 🏈 #BoilerUp @BoilerFootball @PurdueSports @FOXSports pic.twitter.com/m0Yf9exf1h — Boiler Suit Guys (@boilersuitguys) October 17, 2026 2 INTs and 3 pts to show for it, COME ON. — (260) Boiler12 ~🚂 (@260Boiler12) October 17, 2026 Purdue redzone again pic.twitter.com/2Zlgco8r6n — #BoilerUp (@LancerUWM) October 17, 2026 What a run by Harris and some gangster QB blocking and awareness by Browne. What a play! — Paint's Painter (@Paintspainter) October 17, 2026 I’m really close to starting to be mean to Kevin Kane again — Kevin Kane Hater (@JWurminator) October 17, 2026 Touchdown Washington. 5 plays It seems that Kevin Kane might not have fixed things. Illinois and Minnesota are just super ass https://t.co/9d0CtQhhZX — Isaiah Walker (@walkeri141) October 17, 2026 It is genuinely not talked enough about how completely and utterly dogshit big ten refs are at their jobs Abysmal officiating. Embarrassing — Isaiah Walker (@walkeri141) October 17, 2026 He did everything he was supposed to for that not to be roughing the passer. wtf — Kraig Bowers (@kraigbowers34) October 17, 2026 i’ve seen more egregious tackling in big ten basketball go uncalled … https://t.co/l63urzgdcV — chris (@Vuhdo) October 17, 2026 Kevin

item.title: Manuel Neuer participates, but Joshua Kimmich is absent for Bayern Munich training
item.description: (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to a report from Abendzeitung journalist Maximilian Koch , Bayern Munich has received encouraging news ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League showdown against Arsenal. Manuel Neuer participated in the final training session, and Joshua Kimmich is expected to be available despite missing practice. Kimmich missed the session for private reasons, but he is expected to be fit to face Arsenal tomorrow. His availability would be a major boost for Vincent Kompany’s side, as the German international is expected to play a crucial role in Bayern Munich’s attempt to control the midfield against Declan Rice and Arsenal’s talented engine room. Meanwhile, Neuer’s participation in the final training session increases the likelihood that Bayern Munich’s captain will start against the Gunners. The veteran goalkeeper recently returned to team training and was scheduled to undergo a final fitness assessment. His presence on the pitch is an encouraging sign as Bayern Munich prepares for one of its biggest tests of the season. There is still a question mark over Kompany himself. The Bayern Munich head coach was advised to rest due to a viral infection, leaving assistant coach Aaron Danks to lead the session. With kickoff approaching, Bayern Munich will be hoping for positive news on all fronts. Having Neuer between the posts and Kimmich available in midfield would provide valuable expe rience and leadership against an Arsenal side expected to test them in every dep artment. The signs are encouraging for Bayern Munich, but final confirmation will likely come later on Tuesday. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: New, improved notifications system! item.title: Fans erupt after both WNBA Finals teams leave the court for the anthem
item.description: Source: zimmytws/Depositphotos pavelsch/Depositphotos WNBA Finals teams leave court before anthem The Women’s National Basketball Association (WNBA) opened the 2026 Finals on October 17 in San Francisco. Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries players left Chase Center’s court before the anthem. Both rosters were absent while Oakland singer Goapele performed The Star-Spangled Banner. The pregame departure drew criticism after footage appeared online, although neither team immediately offered a reason for leaving. Jean_Nelson/Depositphotos Goapele performs before the Finals opener Goapele, an Oakland singer and songwriter, sang the national anthem before the Finals opener on October 17. Golden State organized a program featuring performers with ties to the Bay Area. Actor Rita Moreno was scheduled to lead the pregame drum ceremony, while San Francisco rapper Larry June was listed for halftime. The entertainment lineup accompanied Golden State’s first Finals appearance. MichaelVi/Depositphotos Dream and Valkyries return within seconds Atlanta and Golden State warmed up at Chase Center before leaving the floor ahead of the anthem. An eyewitness estimated their absence lasted about two minutes, which covered the song’s performance. Players returned within seconds of the final note, jogging back onto the surface before tipoff. The departure happened during pregame activities, rather than during regulation play in the championship opener. Jean_Nelson/Depositphotos WNBA anthem videos capture pregame moments Two videos circulated after the October 17 ceremony at Chase Center in San Francisco. One recording showed Goapele’s anthem performance, while another documented the teams’ movements before the Finals opener. The San Francisco Chronicle shared footage of the performance, while a reporter inside Chase Center posted a separate clip. The recordings allowed viewers to compare different moments from the ceremony. Mojahid_Mottakin/Depositphotos WNBA fans call for penalties after anthem Some X users called for penalties after watching the departure footage. One commenter suggested fines for the clubs, while another urged the arena to repeat the anthem until players stayed. Other online reactions accused the clubs of showing disrespect and criticized the WNBA. The remarks appeared on X following Saturday’s ceremony, adding separate complaints about player conduct and league oversight. zimmytws/Depositphotos Emily Austin criticizes WNBA leadership Sports broadcaster Emily Austin criticized the WNBA after both teams left the court before the anthem. Her social media post argued that off-court controversies distracted from the league’s athletic talent. She also questioned leadership within the league and said its athletes deserved better. Austin’s remarks addressed the surrounding publicity, not the official result or player performances in the Finals opener. zimmytws/Depositphotos WNBA rules describe anthem conduct The WNBA’s 2026 rulebook says players, coach

Austin’s remarks addressed the surrounding publicity, not the official result or player performances in the Finals opener. zimmytws/Depositphotos WNBA rules describe anthem conduct The WNBA’s 2026 rulebook says players, coaches and trainers should stand in a dignified line along the sidelines or foul line during the national anthem. However, AP reported on October 20 that the league had suspended its anthem protocols in 2017. The printed provision alone does not establish that the Finals teams violated an enforceable attendance requirement. Depositphotos Later reporting adds context to the departures OutKick reported on October 19 that the WNBA and both teams had not answered its questions about the Game 1 anthem departures. The outlet said it contacted them on October 17 and followed up the next day. Subsequent AP reporting said that Golden State described its departure as part of its usual pregame routine. AP also reported that Atlanta had been leaving the court before the anthem for several years. galecophoto/Depositphotos Atlanta Dream included union message in 2020 The Atlanta Dream included a Women’s National Basketball Players Association statement in game notes during August 2020. That message explained the union’s concerns about national anthem ceremonies and unequal treatment. The association said the anthem did not represent freedom and justice for every American. During July 2020, the WNBA also announced a joint social justice initiative with its players’ union. lev radin/Shutterstock.com Angel Reese played in a 2024 anthem incident Angel Reese played for Louisiana State University when the team missed the national anthem before facing Iowa on April 1, 2024. The NCAA contest took place in Albany, New York. LSU coach Kim Mulkey said the team customarily left the floor 12 minutes before tipoff. She explained that the group’s absence from the ceremony was unintentional, reflecting its preparation schedule. Fun fact: The Star-Spangled Banner uses a melody originally written for a London gentlemen’s music club in the 1770s, decades before it became America’s national anthem. galecophoto/Depositphotos Caitlin Clark drew anthem comments in August Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham attracted online attention during the national anthem before Indiana faced Atlanta on August 16, 2026. Both Fever players remained on the court for the song. Video showed Cunningham placing a hand over her heart, while Clark stood with both hands behind her back. Some viewers praised Cunningham’s gesture and criticized Clark’s posture during the ceremony. Keeton Gale/Shutterstock.com Valkyries take Game 1 with a 68-64 win The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-64 in the Finals opener Saturday. Gabby Williams scored a game-high 26 points, including 16 during the second quarter at Chase Center. Atlanta made just two of 19 field goal attempts in the fourth quarter. Allisha Gray led the Dream with 19 points, while Angel Reese contributed 14 points and 12 rebounds. A’ja Wilson’s record-breaking MVP season still ended in playoff disappointment. Explore how her historic year took an unexpected turn. im_source/Depositphotos WNBA Finals move to Atlanta with the series tied Atlanta beat Golden State 79–65 in Game 2 at Chase Center on October 19, tying the best-of-7 Finals at 1–1. Angel Reese led the Dream with 30 points and 16 rebounds. Atlanta is scheduled to host Game 3 at State Farm Arena on October 21 at 8 p.m. Eastern. Game 4 follows on October 24 at 1 p.m. Eastern. Game 3 was moved from October 22, while Game 4’s start was advanced from 3:30 p.m. Sophie Cunningham’s reaction has added to the discussion surrounding the controversial no-call involving Angel Reese. Explore more about the play and the debate over the officials’ decision. Should WNBA teams be required to remain on the court during the national anthem, or should players have more flexibility during pregame ceremonies? Share your thoughts in the comments below! This slideshow was made with AI assistance and human editing. With Mike Evans reportedly dealing with Achilles soreness, Kittle could be especially important to the passing attack. His touchdown production gives him a strong ceiling. Week 7 Fantasy Football Sleepers Harold Fannin Jr., CLE (@ TEN) Harold Fannin Jr. enters Week 7 looking to rebound after two consecutive games with just one reception. He managed only one catch for nine yards on three targets in Week 6. That’s a sharp decline from Weeks 2-4, when he averaged five receptions and one touchdown per game. Cleveland’s passing struggles have contributed to the downturn. Deshaun Watson has been held below 175 passing yards in three of his last four games. Fannin is therefore a speculative play rather than a dependable starter. That said, his earlier production suggests there may be more upside if the offense improves. The matchup against Tennessee gives him a chance to regain some momentum. Pat Freiermuth, PIT (@ NO) Pat Freiermuth recorded just two catches for 11 yards on three targets in Week 6. Those numbers offer little immediate fantasy football excitement. Still, his circumstances deserve consideration. Freiermuth played through a calf injury that appeared on the injury report shortly before Sunday’s game. A healthier week of practice could help him become a more reliable option against New Orleans. Managers searching for a tight end alternative should monitor his practice participation. If he returns to full health, he could offer useful depth. Hunter Henry, NE (@ CHI) Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Hunter Henry is the most appealing sleeper of this group. He has found the end zone in consecutive games. He caught four of five targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in Week 6. That continues a productive stretch in which he has recorded at least four targets in four of his last five games. That makes Henry a viable option for managers who need help at tight end. His Week 7 matchup against Chicago offers another opportunity to build on his momentum. While touchdowns are difficult to predict, Henry’s recent usage gives him a clearer path to fantasy relevance. Injury and Late-Week Notes Tyler Warren is dealing with a groin injury, while TJ Hockenson is managing a concussion. Monitor their practice participation and official injury designations before kickoff, as either situation could affect Week 7 lineup decisions. Week 7 Fantasy Football Tight End Rankings 1. Brock Bowers, LV (vs. LAR) 2. Trey McBride, ARI (vs. DEN) 3. George Kittle, SF (@ ATL) 4. Isaiah Likely, NYG (@ HOU) 5. Tucker Kraft, GB (@ DET) 6. Sam LaPorta, DET (vs. GB) 7. Dallas Goedert, PHI (vs. DAL) 8. Travis Kelce, KC (@ SEA) 9. Colston Loveland, CHI (vs. NE) 10. Juwan Johnson, NO (vs. PIT) 11. Kyle Pitts Sr., ATL (vs. SF) 12. Harold Fannin Jr., CLE (@ TEN) 13. T.J. Hockenson, MIN (vs. IND) 14. Tyler Higbee, LAR (@ LV) 15. Pat Freiermuth, PIT (@ NO) 16. Hunter Henry, NE (@ CHI) 17. Colby Parkinson, LAR (@ LV) 18. Darren Waller, CAR (vs. TB) 19. Mark Andrews, BAL (vs. CIN) 20. Dalton Schultz, HOU (vs. NYG) Final Takeaway Bowers, McBride, and Kittle headline the Week 7 rankings. They offer a blend of target volume, consistency, and touchdown upside. Henry is the sleeper to watch after scoring in back-to-back games, while Fannin and Freiermuth carry more uncertainty. Prioritize dependable involvement, check the latest injury updates, and avoid chasing touchdowns alone when making your final tight end decisions. item.title: U2 to headline first-ever NFL Thanksgiving Eve game halftime show
item.description: U2 will perform at the first-ever NFL Thanksgiving Eve game Nov. 25. File Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI Oct. 20 (UPI) -- Irish rock band U2 will headline the first-ever NFL Thanksgiving Eve football game. The NFL announced the news Tuesday ahead of the matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams Nov. 25 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif. The performance will celebrate U2's 50th anniversary as a group. The rock band, fronted by Bono, is known for such singles as "With or Without You" and "I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For." "There's a reason U2 has headline stadiums for decades: they don't just perform, they deliver iconic moments audiences remember forever," Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said in a statement . "We're thrilled that they'll bring that same magic to the NFL stage on Netflix. It's going to be an unforgettable night for football fans and Netflix members worldwide." Bono attends the Cannes Film Festival photocall for "Bono: Stories of Surrender" in 2025. File Photo by Rocco Spaziani/UPI View this post on Instagram Bono attends the Cannes Film Festival premiere of "Bono: Stories of Surrender" in 2025. File Photo by Rocco Spaziani/UPI A post shared by NFL (@nfl) U2 previously headlined the halftime show at Super Bowl XXXVI between the New England Patriots and St. Louis Rams in New Orleans in 2002. The NFL Thanksgiving Eve game will start coverage at 6 p.m. ET on Netflix, with kick off scheduled for 8 p.m.

item.title: Betis Champions League squad: Ruibal returns, Cucho misses out
item.description: Betis Champions League squad: Ruibal returns, Cucho misses out Real Betis have announced their official squad for the decisive Champions League clash against Feyenoord . The Green and Whites will make their final preparations at La Cartuja stadium, with some notable changes to the coaching staff’s squad selection. The big news in the Betis squad is the return of Aitor Ruibal. The versatile player has recovered from his fitness issues, completing the final training session alongside his teammates and making himself fully available to the coach. The downside is the absence of Cucho Hernández. The Colombian striker has been left out of the squad after experiencing discomfort that prevented him from training at the Luis del Sol training ground, joining the already absent Junior Firpo. The rest of the first-team regulars are included in the Green and Whites’ squad as they look to make home advantage count. The presence of key midfield players ensures the tactical solidity needed to keep pace with the Dutch side. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: 1 Bold Prediction for Each Game in NFL Week 7, Including Chiefs-Seahawks
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Even though the last game just ended on Monday, the football calendar moves fast, and now it’s time to look ahead to Week 7, which kicks off on Thursday. With 28 of 32 teams back in action, it’s time to make a bold prediction for all 14 games on the NFL Week 7 schedule. Related: Week 7 NFL Power Rankings: Browns Leap Ahead While Rams Fall Flat Jaylon Johnson Records Two Interceptions in Bears Win Over Patriots Oct 11, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Chicago Bears defensive back Jaylon Johnson (1) reacts after a touchdown by Green Bay Packers during the third quarter at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images Chicago Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson hasn’t performed well since the season kicked off. Limited to just seven games last season due to multiple injuries, Johnson is either still battling injuries or is just a step slower in his seventh season. Yet, this is a three-time Pro Bowler. If Drake Maye tests him often, Johnson has a chance to wake up and record not one, but two interceptions. Related: 6 Khalil Mack Trade Destinations As NFL Rumors Heat Up Jaylen Warren’s 130-Yard, 2 TD Day Lifts Steelers Past Saints Oct 11, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren (30) scores a touchdown in the third quarter against the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Suddenly Jaylen Warren is on fire, and even though Rico Dowdle returned from injury last week, the Pittsburgh Steelers will ride the hot hand. Right now, that’s Warren, who actually entered Week 6 leading the team in rushing and receiving, something that’s never been done in Pittsburgh over the course of a full season. Plenty capable of going off as a rusher while still contributing as a pass-catcher, Warren’s in for a big 130-yard, two-touchdown day against a woeful New Orleans Saints defense that has fallen off a cliff this season. Related: Week 7 NFL Defense Rankings: Eagles Descend and Chiefs Ascend; Week 7 Fantasy D/ST Rankings Vikings Record Six Sacks on Daniel Jones’ Colts Jan 13, 2025; Glendale, AZ, USA; Minnesota Vikings quarterback Daniel Jones (13) against the Los Angeles Rams during an NFC wild card game at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Daniel Jones has fully recovered from last season’s Achilles tear and has started all six games for the Indianapolis Colts in 2026. Yet, one wonders if he’s still battling some mental blocks since his surgery, because he hasn’t been the same player who earned the “Indiana Jones’ moniker while performing as an early-season MVP candidate in 2025. Meanwhile, the Minnesota Vikings’ defense has been the best in the NFL, with Brian Flores blitzing at record rates. Add it all up, and Jones is in for a rough day, the kind that sees him get sacked six times. Related: 5 Minnesota Vikings Trades To Capitalize on 5-0 Start Kyle Pitts’ 100-Yard Game Fuels Falcons to Victory Over 49ers Oct

Still, Willis has displayed his trademark athleticism while being willing to take some shots downfield too. Playing with a big chip on his shoulder, don’t be shocked if Mayfield goes off for a 350-yard day in a big NFC South divisional win for the Bucs over the Panthers. item.title: Who should be the El Paso Girls Athlete of the Week? Cast your vote
item.description: With the 2026-27 high school sports season approaching, the El Paso Times will give readers a chance to vote to select El Paso's top athletes and teams. This week, readers can vote for the Girls Athlete of the Week in volleyball and cross country for the week of Oct. 13-17. Here are this week's nominees. Here are this week's nominees: Casey Saenz, Hanks Volleyball. In the last two victory matches, she had 21 kills, 40 assists, 3 aces, and 15 digs. Carlee Caraveo, Eastwood cross country . Caraveo ran an impressive second place to help the Troopers finish second in the District 1-6A competition. Sayuri Ulloa, Burges cross country. Ulloa won the District 1-5A cross country individual title. Anel Ponce, Parkland cross country. She won her first individual title in District 2-5A cross country with a time of 21:42.96. Mariana Alvarez, Austin cross country . She won the individual title in District 1-4A with a time of 15:10.15. Alexia Martinez, Fabens cross country. She won the individual title at the District 2-4A meet. Maya Bemis, El Paso High volleyball. In victory vs. Canutillo, she had 15 kills, 12 digs and 3 aces. Difanny Soltero, Coronado volleyball. In two matches last week, she had 26 kills, 40 assists and 33 digs. Giselle Gandara, Eastlake volleyball . In two matches last week, she had 32 kills and 17 digs. Davanee Montelongo, El Dorado volleyball. Against Del Valle, she had 21 kills and 27 digs and vs. Parkland, she had seven kills and nine digs. Felix F. Chavez can be reached at fchavez@elpasotimes.com; @Fchavezeptimes on X This article originally appeared on El Paso Times: Who should be the El Paso Girls Athlete of the Week? Cast your vote

item.title: How Many Breeders’ Cup Winners Has Aidan O’Brien Had?
item.description: Aidan O’Brien’s dominance on the global racing stage is unprecedented, and nowhere is his transatlantic genius more evident than at the World Championships. The Ballydoyle maestro stands as the joint-most successful trainer in Breeders’ Cup history, boasting a record-breaking 21 victories with Bob Baffert. From establishing a stronghold on the juvenile turf contests to capturing showpiece events like the Breeders’ Cup Turf, O’Brien’s meticulous preparation has transformed North America’s marquee meeting into a home away from home. Aidan O’Brien’s First Breeders’ Cup Winner: Johannesburg (2001) Before he was the all-time leader, O’Brien landed his breakthrough Breeders’ Cup victory at Belmont Park in 2001 with a special colt named Johannesburg. Having dominated the European two-year-old division over turf-winning the Norfolk, Phoenix, Prix Morny, and Middle Park Stakes-Johannesburg faced an entirely new test in the Breeders’ Cup Juvenile. He was stepping up to a mile and making his debut on dirt against top-class American dirt specialists. Ridden with complete confidence by Mick Kinane, Johannesburg travelled supremely well around the turn, quickened into the straight, and fended off Repent to win by a length and a quarter. To this day, Johannesburg remains O’Brien’s sole Breeders’ Cup victory on dirt-a landmark moment that heralded the arrival of Ballydoyle as a true force in world racing. O’Brien is the joint-Breeders’ Cup trainer with Bob Baffert (21), with the pair one ahead of D. Wayne Lukas, who sadly died in June 2025 (89). Breeders’ Cup wins by trainer Aidan O’Brien – 21 Bob Baffert – 21 D. Wayne Lukas – 20 Chad Brown – 16 Todd A. Pletcher – 15 Aidan O’Brien’s 2025 Breeders’ Cup victories featured: Gstaad (Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Turf): Overcame a wide draw and missed break under Christophe Soumillon to storm late and deliver O’Brien’s record-breaking 21st victory. The Aidan O’Brien Fortress Breeders’ Cup Races: Dominance in the Juvenile Turf and Turf While O’Brien’s 21 Breeders’ Cup titles span multiple divisions, two specific turf contests have become personal domains for Ballydoyle: Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Turf (8 Wins) No trainer comes close to matching O’Brien’s mastery in the Juvenile Turf. Since the race’s inauguration, Ballydoyle has turned it into a springboard for future classic stars. His eight winners demonstrate his uncanny ability to identify two-year-olds with both the class and maturity required for tight American tracks: Wrote (2011) George Vancouver (2012) Hit It A Bomb (2015) Mendelssohn (2017) Victoria Road (2022) Unquestionable (2023) Henri Matisse (2024) Gstaad (2025) Breeders’ Cup Turf (7 Wins) Considered one of the premier Grade 1 contests of the entire meeting. The 1½-mile Breeders’ Cup Turf has been a happy hunting ground for O’Brien’s elite middle-distance runners. His seven victories include legendary names and sensational battles: High Chaparral (2002, and the famous 2003 dead-heat) St Nicholas Abbey (2011) Magic

The Ballydoyle maestro stands as the joint-most successful trainer in Breeders’ Cup history, boasting a record-breaking 21 victories with Bob Baffert. From establishing a stronghold on the juvenile turf contests to capturing showpiece events like the Breeders’ Cup Turf, O’Brien’s meticulous preparation has transformed North America’s marquee meeting into a home away from home. Aidan O’Brien’s First Breeders’ Cup Winner: Johannesburg (2001) Before he was the all-time leader, O’Brien landed his breakthrough Breeders’ Cup victory at Belmont Park in 2001 with a special colt named Johannesburg. Having dominated the European two-year-old division over turf-winning the Norfolk, Phoenix, Prix Morny, and Middle Park Stakes-Johannesburg faced an entirely new test in the Breeders’ Cup Juvenile. He was stepping up to a mile and making his debut on dirt against top-class American dirt specialists. Ridden with complete confidence by Mick Kinane, Johannesburg travelled supremely well around the turn, quickened into the straight, and fended off Repent to win by a length and a quarter. To this day, Johannesburg remains O’Brien’s sole Breeders’ Cup victory on dirt-a landmark moment that heralded the arrival of Ballydoyle as a true force in world racing. O’Brien is the joint-Breeders’ Cup trainer with Bob Baffert (21), with the pair one ahead of D. Wayne Lukas, who sadly died in June 2025 (89). Breeders’ Cup wins by trainer Aidan O’Brien – 21 Bob Baffert – 21 D. Wayne Lukas – 20 Chad Brown – 16 Todd A. Pletcher – 15 Aidan O’Brien’s 2025 Breeders’ Cup victories featured: Gstaad (Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Turf): Overcame a wide draw and missed break under Christophe Soumillon to storm late and deliver O’Brien’s record-breaking 21st victory. The Aidan O’Brien Fortress Breeders’ Cup Races: Dominance in the Juvenile Turf and Turf While O’Brien’s 21 Breeders’ Cup titles span multiple divisions, two specific turf contests have become personal domains for Ballydoyle: Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Turf (8 Wins) No trainer comes close to matching O’Brien’s mastery in the Juvenile Turf. Since the race’s inauguration, Ballydoyle has turned it into a springboard for future classic stars. His eight winners demonstrate his uncanny ability to identify two-year-olds with both the class and maturity required for tight American tracks: Wrote (2011) George Vancouver (2012) Hit It A Bomb (2015) Mendelssohn (2017) Victoria Road (2022) Unquestionable (2023) Henri Matisse (2024) Gstaad (2025) Breeders’ Cup Turf (7 Wins) Considered one of the premier Grade 1 contests of the entire meeting. The 1½-mile Breeders’ Cup Turf has been a happy hunting ground for O’Brien’s elite middle-distance runners. His seven victories include legendary names and sensational battles: High Chaparral (2002, and the famous 2003 dead-heat) St Nicholas Abbey (2011) Magician (2013) Found (2015) Highland Reel (2016) Auguste Rodin (2023) Aidan O’Brien’s Breeders’ Cup Winners by Race A complete breakdown of all 21 Breeders’ Cup victories secured by Aidan O’Brien across his illustrious career: Breeders’ Cup Juvenile (1) – Johannesburg (2001) Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf (2) – Meditate (2022), Lake Victoria (2024) Breeders’ Cup Filly & Mare Turf (1) – Tuesday (2022) Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Turf (8) – Wrote (2011), George Vancouver (2012), Hit It A Bomb (2015), Mendelssohn (2017), Victoria Road (2022), Unquestionable (2023), Henri Matisse (2024), Gstaad (2025) Breeders’ Cup Marathon (1) – Man of Iron (2009) Breeders’ Cup Mile (1) – Order of Australia (2020) Breeders’ Cup Turf (7) – High Chaparral (2002, 2003 DH), St Nicholas Abbey (2011), Magician (2013), Found (2015), Highland Reel (2016), Auguste Rodin (2023) Looking Ahead: The 2026 Breeders’ Cup at Keeneland The 2026 Breeders’ Cup World Championships promise another thrilling spectacle as the event returns to one of American racing’s most revered venues. Dates: Friday, October 30 & Saturday, October 31, 2026 Track / Venue: Keeneland Race Course (Lexington, Kentucky) Total Purse: $34+ million across 14 Grade 1 championship races Aidan O’Brien 2026 Breeders’ Cup Hopes Keeneland’s iconic turf track plays right into Ballydoyle’s hands, and O’Brien brings another loaded squad across the Atlantic as he seeks to expand his record. Here are three of his brightest chances for the 2026 meeting: Great Barrier Reef (Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Turf) O’Brien has won the Juvenile Turf a staggering eight times, and Great Barrier Reef looks poised to make it nine. An impressive winner of the Coventry Stakes at Royal Ascot, the colt proved his durability and high-class engine in Europe’s top autumn trials. O’Brien has made no secret of how highly he rates this colt, identifying him early on as a top-tier performer suited to American turf courses. Precise and Diamond Necklace (Breeders’ Cup Filly & Mare Turf) In the Breeders’ Cup Filly & Mare Turf—a race O’Brien previously claimed in 2022 with Tuesday-Ballydoyle holds a pair of top-class contenders in Precise and Diamond Necklace. Precise, an Irish 1000 Guineas winner, brings classic-winning pedigree and sharp turn-of-foot credentials that make her a natural fit for Keeneland’s tight turf course. Meanwhile, Diamond Necklace, winner of the Nassau Stakes at Goodwood and coming off an outstanding third-place finish in the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe, gives O’Brien a proven, top-tier middle-distance filly. Together, they form a potent two-pronged assault as Ballydoyle looks to capture a second victory in the division. Sun Goddess (Breeders Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf) O’Brien’s record with two-year-old fillies on the grass has soared in recent seasons. Winning two of the last four renewals with Meditate (2022) and Lake Victoria (2024). Headline juvenile Sun Goddess heads to Kentucky as an odds-on favourite to add to that record in the Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf. A record-breaking winner of the Group 1 Cheveley Park Stakes and the Phoenix Stakes against colts. The superstar daughter of Sioux Nation has exhibited an explosive turn of foot across her campaign. With Ryan Moore booked for the drive, her natural speed and tactical versatility make her one of Ballydoyle’s shortest-priced and most anticipated transatlantic bankers. Gstaad (Breeders’ Cup Mile) Returning to the site of his potential sophomore target after claiming the 2025 Juvenile Turf as a two-year-old, Gstaad remains one of Ballydoyle’s premier turf milers. Having already proven his affinity for North American racing conditions. He will be a key player as O’Brien bids to add another Mile trophy to his collection. Which of Aidan O’Brien’s runners do you think has the best chance of finding the winner’s enclosure at Keeneland this year?
