item.title: Detroit Tigers Could Make Shocking Spencer Torkelson Decision for 2027
item.description: The Detroit Tigers could be preparing for one of their most difficult roster decisions of the offseason, and former No. 1 overall pick Spencer Torkelson may be at the center of it. Despite finishing the 2026 season with an impressive offensive surge, there is no guarantee Torkelson will be Detroit’s everyday first baseman when Opening Day arrives in 2027. In fact, a closer examination of his September performance reveals why the Tigers might be hesitant to hand him the job without competition. Torkelson produced outstanding power numbers down the stretch, but he also continued to struggle with one of the biggest weaknesses in his offensive game. That leaves president of baseball operations Scott Harris and manager A.J. Hinch facing an intriguing question: Should Detroit trust Torkelson to play every day, or would a reduced role ultimately make the lineup more productive? Detroit Tigers first baseman Spencer Torkelson (20) celebrates a one run home run against Pittsburgh Pirates during the seventh inning at Comerica Park in Detroit on Friday, Sept. 25, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Spencer Torkelson’s September Numbers Tell Two Different Stories At first glance, Torkelson’s final month looked like a convincing argument that he should remain Detroit’s starting first baseman. He batted .296 with six home runs, 14 RBIs and a remarkable 1.080 OPS in September, providing the kind of offensive production the Tigers desperately needed. However, those impressive numbers came with a significant warning sign. According to Torkelson’s detailed 2026 statistical breakdown , he struck out 29 times in just 71 September at-bats, meaning he recorded a strikeout in approximately 41% of his official at-bats. That doesn’t erase his production, particularly his .432 on-base percentage and .648 slugging percentage during the month. But it does suggest that even when Torkelson is producing at an extremely high level, his swing-and-miss tendencies remain a concern. For the season, Torkelson finished with 26 home runs, 77 RBIs and a 113 OPS+, making him an above-average offensive player overall. Those are useful numbers, but Detroit must decide whether they’re enough to justify an everyday role at a position traditionally expected to provide significant offensive production. The question becomes even more complicated when considering the Tigers’ younger alternatives. Detroit Tigers Could Create a Three-Way Competition at First Base Torkelson’s biggest competition may come from players already in the organization rather than an expensive free-agent addition. Colt Keith has emerged as another option at first base, while highly regarded prospect Josue Briceño could push for major-league opportunities during the 2027 season. As we previously examined , Briceño’s path to playing time could run directly through the Tigers’ first-base situation. Despite finishing the 2026 season with an impressive offensive surge, there is no guarantee Torkelson will be Detroit’s everyday first baseman when Opening Day arrives in 2027. In fact, a closer examination of his September performance reveals why the Tigers might be hesitant to hand him the job without competition. Torkelson produced outstanding power numbers down the stretch, but he also continued to struggle with one of the biggest weaknesses in his offensive game. That leaves president of baseball operations Scott Harris and manager A.J. Hinch facing an intriguing question: Should Detroit trust Torkelson to play every day, or would a reduced role ultimately make the lineup more productive? Detroit Tigers first baseman Spencer Torkelson (20) celebrates a one run home run against Pittsburgh Pirates during the seventh inning at Comerica Park in Detroit on Friday, Sept. 25, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Spencer Torkelson’s September Numbers Tell Two Different Stories At first glance, Torkelson’s final month looked like a convincing argument that he should remain Detroit’s starting first baseman. He batted .296 with six home runs, 14 RBIs and a remarkable 1.080 OPS in September, providing the kind of offensive production the Tigers desperately needed. However, those impressive numbers came with a significant warning sign. According to Torkelson’s detailed 2026 statistical breakdown , he struck out 29 times in just 71 September at-bats, meaning he recorded a strikeout in approximately 41% of his official at-bats. That doesn’t erase his production, particularly his .432 on-base percentage and .648 slugging percentage during the month. But it does suggest that even when Torkelson is producing at an extremely high level, his swing-and-miss tendencies remain a concern. For the season, Torkelson finished with 26 home runs, 77 RBIs and a 113 OPS+, making him an above-average offensive player overall. Those are useful numbers, but Detroit must decide whether they’re enough to justify an everyday role at a position traditionally expected to provide significant offensive production. The question becomes even more complicated when considering the Tigers’ younger alternatives. Detroit Tigers Could Create a Three-Way Competition at First Base Torkelson’s biggest competition may come from players already in the organization rather than an expensive free-agent addition. Colt Keith has emerged as another option at first base, while highly regarded prospect Josue Briceño could push for major-league opportunities during the 2027 season. As we previously examined , Briceño’s path to playing time could run directly through the Tigers’ first-base situation. With Dillon Dingler established behind the plate, Detroit may eventually need to find another position for the young catching prospect. That creates several possible lineup combinations for Hinch. Torkelson could remain the primary first baseman, share the position with Keith, or see additional time at designated hitter as Detroit evaluates its emerging hitters. The most surprising possibility would be Torkelson entering spring training without an unquestioned claim to the starting job. Such a move would represent a significant change for a player Detroit selected first overall in the 2020 MLB Draft, but the organization has already shown a willingness to adjust his playing time. According to Detroit’s offseason roster assessment , Torkelson moved into a part-time role late in 2026 while younger players received extended opportunities. His strong September finish complicated that evaluation, but it didn’t eliminate the need to determine the team’s best long-term alignment. Scott Harris Faces a Decision That Goes Beyond Torkelson’s Bat Harris has publicly expressed confidence that Torkelson can help Detroit return to the postseason. However, that endorsement does not necessarily guarantee the same role Torkelson has held throughout much of his major-league career. As we previously reported following Harris’ comments , the Tigers continue to value Torkelson’s production and his presence in the clubhouse. The organization has not announced plans to trade him, release him or remove him from the starting lineup. In fact, keeping Torkelson makes sense from several perspectives. He remains under team control, offers legitimate power, and demonstrated in September that he can still carry the offense for stretches. But Detroit also cannot ignore the continued strikeout problem or the need to develop younger players. With Keith and Briceño creating additional options, Hinch may have an opportunity to build a more flexible first-base rotation rather than relying exclusively on one player. That could mean fewer plate appearances for Torkelson, a different defensive assignment for Keith, or a gradual introduction of Briceño once he proves ready for major-league pitching. None of those outcomes has been announced, but all are reasonable possibilities as Detroit prepares for spring training. Spencer Torkelson’s final month gave the Tigers plenty of reasons to believe in his offensive potential. His underlying numbers also gave them reasons to remain cautious. The shocking decision wouldn’t necessarily be moving on from Torkelson altogether. It could be deciding that one of Detroit’s most recognizable former top prospects must compete for an everyday job in 2027.

South Africa vs. Australia 2nd Test: Day 1 updates At Stumps: South Africa 20/2 Persistent rain washed out the remainder of the opening day at St George's Park, with play officially called off and stumps drawn with South Africa locked at 20/2 in 11.5 overs. Scott Boland produced a sensational double-strike in the 9th over, removing both Aiden Markram and David Bedingham on consecutive deliveries to leave South Africa reeling at 20/2 in 11.5 overs before another persistent band of rain forced the players off the field on Day 1 at St George's Park. Rain Brings Early Lunch: South Africa 11/0 At 12:27 PM, steady rain forced the players off the field. Debutant Marques Ackerman provided a heartwarming scene as the covers came on, waving to his family gathered in the stands as he headed toward the pavilion. Officials quickly opted to take an early lunch at 12:37 PM to prevent further lost game time. South Africa's opening pair safely absorbed the initial test with composure. Australia struggled to find consistent rhythm with the new ball, offering loose deliveries and generating little swing or seam movement off a relatively placid surface. By 1:00 PM, conditions improved sharply as the clouds parted. Ground staff swiftly removed the protective tarpaulins and the umpires re-stumped the pitch, confirming a quick turnaround for the extended afternoon stretch. Matt Renshaw was the star of that win with 190 and 82, and Josh Hazlewood took 6/49 in the second innings. South Africa have made changes following the defeat. Tristan Stubbs has been dropped to make room for Matthew Breetzke, Kagiso Rabada is expected to return after missing the first Test with a hamstring injury, and Ryan Rickelton will keep wicket for the hosts. England Batting Updates 10 overs: England 65/0 (Ben Duckett 29, Tom Banton 35) Tom Banton took on the Pakistan pacers early, launching two sixes alongside four boundaries to strike at over 124. Ben Duckett complemented him from the other end, using his trademark sweeps and cuts through the off side to strike six fours. While Shaheen Shah Afridi maintained relative control (5-0-25-0), Naseem Shah was targeted heavily by both openers, conceding 36 runs across his four overs at an economy rate of 9.00. Having crossed 50 in just 7.6 overs, England completed mandatory Powerplay 1 at 65/0. With the ball sliding on under lights and dew starting to play a factor, the required run rate has dipped below 6.00 per over (5.95), giving England complete control entering Powerplay 2. Jamie Overton broke the 78-run stand on the penultimate ball of the 40th over, bowling Nawaz for an entertaining 79 off 74 balls (5 fours, 4 sixes) to conclude his 10-over spell with tidy figures of 1/38. 30 overs: Pakistan 147/5 (Nawaz 39, Minhas 6) Pakistan are in trouble as they have lost half of their side within the first 30 overs. England bowlers continue to dominate at Rawalpindi as Gus Atkinson spearhead the attack against the hosts. 10 overs: Pakistan 46/2 (Babar 26, Saad Baig 9) Pakistan reached 46/2 after 10 overs against England. Gus Atkinson delivered a dream start for England by removing Fakhar Zaman caught by Joe Root on the very first ball of the match. Sonny Baker later struck to dismiss Saim Ayub for 8, leaving Pakistan under early pressure. Babar Azam has worked hard to anchor the innings, moving to 26 off 41 balls. He found a steady partner in debutant Saad Baig (9* off 12), who managed to relieve some pressure by dispatching Gus Atkinson for consecutive boundaries in the final over of the powerplay. Will Jacks kept things tight during a quiet ninth over as Pakistan look to rebuild through the middle phase. Toss result: England won the toss and elected to bowl first, so Pakistan will bat first. Salman Ali Agha hit 107, Babar Azam added 45 and debutant Saad Baig made 39, while Shaheen Shah Afridi took three wickets as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 268. England are playing their first match of the tri-series and their first ODI series in Pakistan since 2005. Harry Brook's side arrive after a 2-1 series win over Sri Lanka, sealed by a 223-run victory at The Oval, where Tom Banton made 126. item.title: What time is Sixers game tonight? LeBron James, Sixers opener vs. Knicks
item.description: It still might not seem real, but NBA legend LeBron James will finally make his Philadelphia 76ers debut tonight as the Sixers tipoff off the 2026-2027 season against the reigning champion New York Knicks . Along with James, former Boston Celtics star Jaylen Brown also is set to appear in a Sixers jersey for the first time following a shocked offseason trade that sent Paul George and picks to the Celtics. The two All-NBA forwards will be joined by Sixers stars Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and V.J. Edgecombe as Philly looks to ruin the NBA-title banner night for Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns and the rest of the Knicks and their fans. Here's how to watch: When is the Sixers first game? The Philadelphia 76ers will take on the New York Knicks to open the season on Oct. 20. Is LeBron James playing tonight? James is set to make his regular season NBA debut with the 76ers tonight against the Knicks. What time is Sixers game tonight? The Sixers-Knicks season opener will tipoff at 7 p.m. ET. What channel is the Sixers game tonight? The Sixers-Knicks season opener will be broadcast on nationally. Here's how to watch: TV: NBC Streaming: Peacock 76ers injury report Dean Wade: Questionable (ankle) Adem Bona: Questionable (foot) Anfernee Simons: Questionable (hamstring) Tacko Fall: Out (hip) Dominick Barlow: Out (Likely to miss two weeks with lumbar spine bone stress response) Knicks injury report No injuries to report Projected Sixers starting lineup with LeBron James With James signing with Philadelphia, the Sixers would potentially have one of the most talented starting lineups in the NBA. Here's what it might look it: Sixers potential starting lineup Joel Embiid, C LeBron James, PF Jaylon Brown, SF V.J. As part of a deal with former 76ers and current Fanatics owner Michael Rubin, James has unlimited access to use a helicopter to take flights back and forth from NYC to games in Philly. What jersey number will LeBron James wear with the Sixers? The Sixers made it official on July 27 that James will wear No. 23. How old is LeBron James? James is 41 years old and is entering his 24th season in the NBA. He will turn 42 years old on Dec. 30. When are Sixers on National TV? The acquisition of James has put the franchise back in the NBA spotlight. This season, Philadelphia will play a franchise-record and league-maximum 34 nationally televised games. Here's a look at some of the featured matchups: Opening night: Philadelphia 76ers at New York Knicks, 7 p.m. Oct. 20 Home opener: Cleveland Cavaliers at Philadelphia 76

item.title: Who should be the El Paso Boys Athlete of the Week? Cast your vote
item.description: With the 2026-27 high school sports season approaching, the El Paso Times will give readers a chance to vote to select El Paso's top athletes and teams. This week, readers can vote for the Boys Athlete of the Week in football and cross country for the week of Oct. 13-17. Here are this week's nominees. Here are this week's nominees: David Retana, Harmony Science Academy cross country. He won the District 1-4A cross country title. Armando Jalil, Clint cross country. He won the District 2-4A individual title with a time of 16:58.44. Jordan Diaz, Del Valle cross country. Diaz won the individual championship in District 2-5A with a time of 17:76.70. Andrew Truax, El Paso High cross country. Truax repeated as the individual district champion in 1-5A with a time of 17:00.73. Noah Garcia, Eastwood cross country. Garcia won the District 1-6A title as an individual. D'Angelo Garcia, Irvin football . In win vs. Fabens, he rushed for 151 yards and on defense, he had 12 tackles and a fumble recovery for a score. Juel Delgado, Chapin football. In win vs. Burges, he had 14 tackles, one interception, three sacks and two pass breakups. Aavant Clayton, Andress football. In win vs. Riverside, Clayton scored five touchdowns. AJ Guzman, Ysleta football . In win vs. Austin, he caught a touchdown pass and returned an interception for a score. Aiden Nunez, Parkland football. Against Bel air, he threw three TD passes and rushed for a TD. He also had four total scores. Felix F. Chavez cabe reached at fchavez@elpasotimes.com; @Fchavezeptimes on X This article originally appeared on El Paso Times: Who should be the El Paso Boys Athlete of the Week? Cast your vote

item.title: Arizona State coach Kenny Dillingham speaks out on fans ‘losing their minds’ amid slow start
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Arizona State coach Kenny Dillingham speaks out on fans ‘losing their minds’ amid slow start appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Arizona State has struggled somewhat this year. They just fell to Texas Tech, dropping their third game of the season. J’Koby Williams of Texas Tech dominated on the ground as the Red Raiders won 53-25. Now, head coach Kenny Dillingham is talking about the loss, being asked about fans “losing their minds” by Jakob Brook of SunDevilSource.com. “I told my family the entire time, ‘You guys realize eventually this is going to turn.’ It’s the nature of the coaching profession. You’ve just gotta be ready for it. When your highs are so high, your lows are gonna be so low. You can’t get upset or frustrated. Nobody cares what you did yesterday, they care what you do now. It doesn’t bother me,” Dillingham said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Dillingham took over at Arizona State for the 2023 season, inheriting a program in disarray. They went 3-9 that season, but Dillingham quickly turned things around. The Sun Devils went 11-3 the next year, winning the Big 12 and making a run to the College Football Playoff. They earned the four seed, but fell in the quarterfinal to Texas in double overtime. It was a slight drop-off in 2025, going 8-5 and finishing fourth in the conference. This year, Arizona State is just 1-2 in conference play and has lost both of their games this season against ranked opponents. The schedule does not get any easier either. They host Kansas State next week, but have trips to BYU and Arizona on the calendar, as well as a home date with Oklahoma State. Regardless of the difficulty coming up, Dillingham seems to be unfazed as he prepares for the rest of the season. Related: Urban Meyer calls out ‘perplexing’ QB decision by Ohio State’s Ryan Day Related: Former Auburn Linebacker Xavier Atkins breaks silence after dismissal

item.title: Joe Mazzulla Sets Bold Goal That Could Define Celtics' Season
item.description: Joe Mazzulla Sets Bold Goal That Could Define Celtics' Season originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Joe Mazzulla's vision for the Boston Celtics this season is clear. Ahead of Tuesday's season opener against the Detroit Pistons, the Celtics shared the first episode of their "Celtics: Way of Life" series documenting the 2026-27 NBA season. The video included a message Mazzulla shared to the team while they were in Charleston, South Carolina. "I do know the pace that we're on from a connectivity standpoint is a separating factor, and that's what we're trying to get to — the most connected team under the highest amount of duress, not just when it's going well," Mazzulla said . Mazzulla's push for the Celtics to become the NBA's most connected team started long before training camp. Not only did Mazzulla visit several players at their homes, but players spent time with each other throughout the offseason. MORE: Why Paul George Is Ready to Rediscover All-Star Form After Celtics-76ers Trade The emphasis on connectivity is particularly notable for a Celtics team entering a new era after losing its longest-tenured player. Boston, of course, traded Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers for Paul George and multiple draft picks in the offseason. Additionally, the Celtics picked up Mike Conley and Mitchell Robinson in free agency. The three veterans bring significant experience to a team that will need to build chemistry quickly. George is a nine-time All-Star looking to win his first NBA championship. Conley is entering his 20th NBA season and has built a reputation as one of the league's best teammates. Robinson is a nine-year rebounding machine coming off a championship with the New York Knicks. For a team with several new pieces, Mazzulla believes connectivity could be what separates the Celtics from the rest of the league. item.title: Demichelis hails Diomande ahead of Real Madrid winger’s reunion with RB Leipzig
item.description: Demichelis hails Diomande ahead of Real Madrid winger’s reunion with RB Leipzig RB Leipzig coach Martin Demichelis has hailed Yan Diomande’s potential ahead of the 19-year-old winger’s reunion with his former club in Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Real Madrid. Demichelis had little time to work with Diomande after taking charge of Leipzig in July, with the winger completing a big-money move to Real Madrid shortly afterwards. Nevertheless, the Argentine has seen enough to be convinced of the youngster’s immense potential. “I predict a great future for him because his development here was very significant. Leipzig are a club that do a great deal to accelerate the development of young players with enormous potential,” said Demichelis in an interview with AS. “Football has increasingly moved towards using extremely dangerous wingers who can beat their opponents one-on-one, and Yan is one of those players who currently make a difference. He can play on either flank because he has excellent control of the ball with both feet, as well as outstanding acceleration over very short distances,” he added. “You also have to appreciate that he is one of the wingers who works hardest defensively. At a great institution like Real Madrid, his development will depend on how he continues to progress. I have no doubt that he will have excellent coaches and teammates, but ultimately, a lot will depend on him and his desire to keep improving.” Wednesday’s encounter at the Estadio Santiago Bernabéu is also set to see Real Madrid centre-back Ibrahima Konaté face his former club, with kick-off scheduled for 21:00 CEST.

item.title: Antoine Griezmann gets ‘two or three more years’ MLS prediction as legendary French forward shares Florida sunshine with fellow World Cup winner Lionel Messi
item.description: Antoine Griezmann Lionel Messi MLS 2026 - Getty/GOAL Griezmann working on a contract until 2028 Griezmann, who captured a global title with France in 2018 and earned 137 caps for his country, decided to go chasing the American dream in the summer of 2026. Having starred across two spells at Atletico Madrid, which were sandwiched around a stint at Barcelona, the mercurial playmaker decided that he was ready for a completely new challenge. Orlando were happy to throw open their doors and have seen a marquee addition make a positive early impact - with 13 goals being recorded through 18 appearances in all competitions. Griezmann signed a contract until 2028, with those terms including the option for a further 12-month extension. Grimandi is confident that his fellow countryman will honour that full agreement. There has been no sign of the Atleti legend slowing down. He will turn 36 in March 2027, but has never been a player that relied on pace over the turf. His sporting intelligence has allowed him to thrive, and those qualities remain on full display in the States. How long will World Cup winner Griezmann play for? How long will World Cup winner Griezmann play for? Grimandi, who signed for the Colorado Rapids in 2003 on the back of stints at Monaco and Arsenal but never made an appearance for the Denver-based outfit, told GOAL - while speaking in association with Swiper Casino Canada - when asked how long Griezmann can play for: “He scored two goals this weekend, he gave an assist again, so he's performed very well. “Griezmann has lost a bit his physical ability, but he's so intelligent and technically he's top so he can still perform. He looks after his body well, he still has good stamina. When you are intelligent and you have good technique you can play long. “Griezmann I think is the ‘91 generation, so he has two or three more years to play if he still wants to do it. Physically and technically, with his intelligence, he can do it without any problems.” Can anyone stop Messi winning another MLS MVP award? Griezmann was a team-mate of Argentine GOAT Messi at Barcelona . He is now a direct rival of the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner and one of those that continues to be amazed by the level of performance produced by an evergreen 39-year-old. Messi is leading the MLS Golden Boot race again, with 25 goals to his name, and should be a serious contender for a record-extending third successive MVP award . item.content:encoded: Antoine Griezmann Lionel Messi MLS 2026 - Getty/GOAL Griezmann working on a contract until 2028 Griezmann, who captured a global title with France in 2018 and earned 137 caps for his country, decided to go chasing the American dream in the summer of 2026. Having starred across two spells at Atletico Madrid, which were sandwiched around a stint at Barcelona, the mercurial playmaker decided that he was ready for a completely new challenge. Orlando were happy to throw open their doors and have seen a marquee addition make a positive early impact - with 13 goals being recorded through 18 appearances in all competitions. Griezmann signed a contract until 2028, with those terms including the option for a further 12-month extension. Grimandi is confident that his fellow countryman will honour that full agreement. There has been no sign of the Atleti legend slowing down. He will turn 36 in March 2027, but has never been a player that relied on pace over the turf. His sporting intelligence has allowed him to thrive, and those qualities remain on full display in the States. How long will World Cup winner Griezmann play for? How long will World Cup winner Griezmann play for? Grimandi, who signed for the Colorado Rapids in 2003 on the back of stints at Monaco and Arsenal but never made an appearance for the Denver-based outfit, told GOAL - while speaking in association with Swiper Casino Canada - when asked how long Griezmann can play for: “He scored two goals this weekend, he gave an assist again, so he's performed very well. “Griezmann has lost a bit his physical ability, but he's so intelligent and technically he's top so he can still perform. He looks after his body well, he still has good stamina. When you are intelligent and you have good technique you can play long. “Griezmann I think is the ‘91 generation, so he has two or three more years to play if he still wants to do it. Physically and technically, with his intelligence, he can do it without any problems.” Can anyone stop Messi winning another MLS MVP award? Griezmann was a team-mate of Argentine GOAT Messi at Barcelona . He is now a direct rival of the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner and one of those that continues to be amazed by the level of performance produced by an evergreen 39-year-old. Messi is leading the MLS Golden Boot race again, with 25 goals to his name, and should be a serious contender for a record-extending third successive MVP award . Asked if anybody can stop the South American superstar, Grimandi said: “When you talk about the Ballon d'Or, sometimes I said maybe they're going to give it to him just for all he has done in his career and still finish in the World Cup final, still finish MVP. “I said why not because at his age what he's still doing it's unbelievable. Every time I have a chance to watch him play live, he's still an exceptional player and it's really amazing to see at this level. “Even if he went through a hard time because he lost his dad, he still performed well and he still has a hunger to win and that's surprising at his age. The last game with Argentina was an emotional moment and it's a chance for football to honour this kind of player.” Griezmann & Messi both starring in the Sunshine State Griezmann & Messi both starring in the Sunshine State Messi bid an emotional farewell to the Argentina national team on October 6. He headed into international retirement with 208 caps to his name. He bowed out with two more assists being added to his tally, along with goal number 126. He is also working on a deal in Florida through 2028 , meaning that his path should cross with Griezmann on a regular basis in the years to come - with both Inter Miami and Orlando City hoping to savour MLS Cup glory in 2026 as the play-offs loom into view.

item.title: Position grades from the Patriots’ win over the Jets
item.description: They can’t all be blowouts, can they? Coming off a convincing 45-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, the New England Patriots found themselves in a much more competitive game versus the New York Jets. A big reason for the game’s comparatively close nature was the Patriots’ own inability to play consistent football between turnovers, dropped passes and uneven run defense. At the end of the day, they still managed to do enough to secure a 26-19 win and improve to 4-2 on the season. It wasn’t overly pretty, but it was still winning football at the end of the day. Let’s take a look at the film and hand out some grades. Patriots film review from NFL Week 6 Quarterback: The typically blitz-heavy Jets decided to alter their approach against Drake Maye, playing a less aggressive form of defense while simultaneously trying to contain him as best they could. They did a solid job, but at the end of the day New England’s quarterback was simply better. Maye delivered some good throws throughout the day, took what the defense gave him, showed some anticipation (see: 3rd-and-10 throw to Kyle Williams), made sound decisions, and once again played at a consistently high level both when throwing the ball and picking his spots to advance it with his legs. His 0.39 expected points added per play are a reflection of that. | Grade: A Running back: Rhamondre Stevenson averaged only 2.6 yards per carry, but he did what he could: he forced four missed tackles and finished with 36 yards after contact on 36 total rushing yards. He also continued to do some good work as a pass protector, giving up one hurry in 11 reps. TreVeyon Henderson played a limited role after suffering an ankle sprain last week, but he mostly moved well and again showed that he is at his best when operating in space. He did lose a fumble, though, which might have contributed to Corey Kiner seeing some action late . Romeo Doubs got open for a 42-yard touchdown on the second snap of the day, but suffered a game-ending shoulder injury along the way. DeMario Douglas led the team with seven catches for 86 yards and a touchdown, but he also lost a fumble when somewhat unnecessarily trying to turn a big play into an even bigger one. Kyle Williams caught just one pass, but it was a big one and showed he can do more than just run go routes. Efton Chism played the second-most snaps among the group but did not finish with any catches while also being uneven as a run blocker. And then, there was A.J. Brown. Coming off a convincing 45-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, the New England Patriots found themselves in a much more competitive game versus the New York Jets. A big reason for the game’s comparatively close nature was the Patriots’ own inability to play consistent football between turnovers, dropped passes and uneven run defense. Let’s take a look at the film and hand out some grades. They did a solid job, but at the end of the day New England’s quarterback was simply better. His 0.39 expected points added per play are a reflection of that. | Grade: A Running back: Rhamondre Stevenson averaged only 2.6 yards per carry, but he did what he could: he forced four missed tackles and finished with 36 yards after contact on 36 total rushing yards. He also continued to do some good work as a pass protector, giving up one hurry in 11 reps. TreVeyon Henderson played a limited role after suffering an ankle sprain last week, but he mostly moved well and again showed that he is at his best when operating in space. He did lose a fumble, though, which might have contributed to Corey Kiner seeing some action late . Kiner hit the holes hard and kept the legs churning through contact. | Grade: A- Fantastic rep by #Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson in pass pro passing off this stunt with LT Will Campbell and completely eliminating Will McDonald's loop. pic.twitter.com/eUypawhA6E — Evan Lazar (@ezlazar) October 19, 2026 Wide receiver: The Patriots’ wide receiver group had a rollercoaster day. Romeo Doubs got open for a 42-yard touchdown on the second snap of the day, but suffered a game-ending shoulder injury along the way. DeMario Douglas led the team with seven catches for 86 yards and a touchdown, but he also lost a fumble when somewhat unnecessarily trying to turn a big play into an even bigger one. Kyle Williams caught just one pass, but it was a big one and showed he can do more than just run go routes. Efton Chism played the second-most snaps among the group but did not finish with any catches while also being uneven as a run blocker. And then, there was A.J. Brown. Making his return from a four-week stint on injured reserve, the veteran was rusty particularly as a finisher: he had two drops and multiple other close calls while catching only three passes for 27 yards. On the bright side, he did manage to get open a lot. Drake Maye targeting Brown 10 times was therefore not a case of force-feeding him; throwing to him was the right read more often than not. | Grade: C+ Tight end: Hunter Henry continues to be one of the most reliable players on the Patriots’ roster, especially as a receiver. He showed good wiggle on a 16-yard catch-and-run on the final drive of the first half, and was able to get wide open on his 7-yard touchdown catch. His run blocking was not quite as consistent (one stuff, one penalty). Eli Raridon also had his ups and downs. He did make a nice adjustment on an 11-yard catch in the third quarter, but could have held onto a touchdown in the late second; he also was at the point of attack on a pair of stuffed runs, but performed well as a move blocker. The same is true for Cameron Latu. | Grade: B+ Offensive line: Even though it lost three starters due to injury during the game, the Patriots offensive line generally played at a high level against a defense that had averaged 3.4 sacks per game coming in. Drake Maye was kept clean for much of the day, with the Jets taking him down not even once. Then, late in the game, the unit — using third-string left guard Walter Rouse and fourth-string right guard Matt Pryor — asserted its will in the run game: the group controlled the line of scrimmage, allowing Corey Kiner to keep advancing the ball on eight straight plays. That said, the performance had its moments but was not consistent, especially on the interior. Run blocking was a concern even before the injuries, and both Rouse and center Jared Wilson had a few bad reps between them down the stretch. On the bright side, Will Campbell played some quality football despite nursing a knee injury, while Caleb Lomu mostly performed well after entering for an injured Morgan Moses. With Campbell and Lomu in the fold, the future seems bright at that position for New England. | Grade: B+ Will Campbell 'influence' vs Enagbare 💪 pic.twitter.com/6SuHgF9JhX — Brandon Thorn (@BrandonThornNFL) October 19, 2026 Defensive line: The Jets were able to create some movement on the line of scrimmage, and exploit New England’s defense for multiple long runs. Looking at the film, however, it appeared to be less of a performance issue and more of New York doing its homework and being able to use Zak Kuhr’s aggressive approach against him and his defense. There were still problems with misplacement and disengagement, but the Patriots’ talent up front also shone through on multiple occasions. That included Milton Williams and Christian Barmore registering back-to-back sacks — the second featuring a dominant bull-rushing rep from Barmore — while rotational backups Cory Durden, DaQuan Jones and Leonard Taylor had some good moments too. The edge trio of Elijah Ponder, Gabe Jacas and Dre’Mont Jones also continued to be disruptive. Jones was at his best setting an edge in the run game, but was a bit more quiet as a pass rusher. Ponder and Jacas flashed their varied skillsets on multiple reps. | Grade: B One of a couple reps where Gabe Jacas swam Jelani Woods into the void Can make TEs look bad with power or finesse pic.twitter.com/QI6FGAHe1A — Taylor Kyles (@tkyles39) October 19, 2026 Linebacker: Robert Spillane continues to be the glue that holds the operation together, and one of the most impactful players on the Patriots roster. His run stuff on 4th-and-2 in the early second quarter against a charging Braelon Allen was an impressive display of his ability to hunker down and hold the line. He also was effective as a run blitzer on multiple occasion. He finished the game with three run stuffs, compared to two by his running mate Christian Elliss. They both had missed tackles as well, and also contributed to the Jets finding success with their turning-the-aggressiveness-against-the-defense plan, but on the whole had a quality outing. | Grade: A – Cornerback: Christian Gonzalez did give up four catches for 45 yards on the day, but only two of those for 20 combined yards came against the Jets’ top receiver. Going up against Garrett Wilson on 17 reps, the Patriots’ No. 1 cornerback more than held his own and forced quarterback Geno Smith to look away from his favorite target repeatedly. Another good outing against a top-tier player. Elsewhere at cornerback, Marcus Jones had a very good day in the office playing both outside and in the slot; he allowed just two passes to be completed to his part of the field. Charles Woods, who again filled in for Carlton Davis as a perimeter corner opposite Gonzalez, looked as good as you would expect a backup to look: there were some hiccups staying with his responsibilities out of bunch formations, but he mostly was well-positioned including on his interception — a play that allowed him to dust off the old receiver skills . | Grade: A Safety: Kevin Byard and Craig Woodson ha

item.title: From gravel to grass: FIFA’s record investments empower emerging football nations
item.description: From gravel to grass: FIFA’s record investments empower emerging football nations Through significantly increased funding and expanded tournament access, developing football markets like Mauritania, Bangladesh, and Bhutan are building sustainable, long-term sporting structures. For many emerging football nations, FIFA represents the primary, if not sole, reliable source of footballing income. Recent financial data and policy shifts indicate a concentrated effort by the governing body to build sustainable structures in these markets, focusing on a triad of financial support, talent development, and expanded tournament access. The financial progression is clear. Under the FIFA Forward programme, funding for each Member Association has grown from around $1 million (before 2016) over $3.8 million (2016-2018 cycle) to $8 million in the current 2023-2026 cycle. A new proposal currently on the table for the 2027-2030 cycle aims to grant associations a total of $25 million each. Ahmed Yahya, President of the Mauritanian Football Federation, noted the practical impact of these numbers following a recent FIFA Council meeting. “These financial resources can enable young people today to play football on grass pitches rather than on stony or gravel-covered pitches, and that is precisely what matters,” Yahya explained. He highlighted the fundamental importance of equal funding and voting rights across all nations. “For us, equality is what defines FIFA today. Gianni Infantino is taking football forward worldwide... The majority want [him] to stay.” Crucially, this financial backing is being paired with the FIFA Talent Development Scheme and an expansion of youth tournaments. By helping associations identify and train talent while simultaneously offering more platforms on the global stage, FIFA is attempting to create a structure where football becomes a genuine career path in developing regions. In Bangladesh, this combined strategy is yielding tangible outcomes. Tabith Awal, President of the Bangladesh Football Federation, pointed to recent milestones, including a historic victory over San Marino during a European window and an invitation to the FIFA ASEAN Cup. “We have used a lot of FIFA’s good projects, whether it be the Arena Programme or the Forward Programme, to truly develop a football culture in Bangladesh,” Awal stated. Awal also highlighted the practical governance style of the current administration, noting that Infantino “continues to show the hands of friendship” even when facing administrative disagreements. A recent brief stopover by the FIFA President in Dhaka allowed local officials to demonstrate exactly how international funds are being allocated on the ground. item.content:encoded: From gravel to grass: FIFA’s record investments empower emerging football nations Through significantly increased funding and expanded tournament access, developing football markets like Mauritania, Bangladesh, and Bhutan are building sustainable, long-term sporting structures. For many emerging football nations, FIFA represents the primary, if not sole, reliable source of footballing income. Recent financial data and policy shifts indicate a concentrated effort by the governing body to build sustainable structures in these markets, focusing on a triad of financial support, talent development, and expanded tournament access. The financial progression is clear. Under the FIFA Forward programme, funding for each Member Association has grown from around $1 million (before 2016) over $3.8 million (2016-2018 cycle) to $8 million in the current 2023-2026 cycle. A new proposal currently on the table for the 2027-2030 cycle aims to grant associations a total of $25 million each. Ahmed Yahya, President of the Mauritanian Football Federation, noted the practical impact of these numbers following a recent FIFA Council meeting. “These financial resources can enable young people today to play football on grass pitches rather than on stony or gravel-covered pitches, and that is precisely what matters,” Yahya explained. He highlighted the fundamental importance of equal funding and voting rights across all nations. “For us, equality is what defines FIFA today. Gianni Infantino is taking football forward worldwide... The majority want [him] to stay.” Crucially, this financial backing is being paired with the FIFA Talent Development Scheme and an expansion of youth tournaments. By helping associations identify and train talent while simultaneously offering more platforms on the global stage, FIFA is attempting to create a structure where football becomes a genuine career path in developing regions. In Bangladesh, this combined strategy is yielding tangible outcomes. Tabith Awal, President of the Bangladesh Football Federation, pointed to recent milestones, including a historic victory over San Marino during a European window and an invitation to the FIFA ASEAN Cup. “We have used a lot of FIFA’s good projects, whether it be the Arena Programme or the Forward Programme, to truly develop a football culture in Bangladesh,” Awal stated. Awal also highlighted the practical governance style of the current administration, noting that Infantino “continues to show the hands of friendship” even when facing administrative disagreements. A recent brief stopover by the FIFA President in Dhaka allowed local officials to demonstrate exactly how international funds are being allocated on the ground. This strategy of global visibility extends to Bhutan, which recently welcomed a FIFA President on its soil for the first time in history. The visit underscored a broader administrative objective to maintain direct contact with all Member Associations, regardless of size, and allowed local leadership to map out the future. Dasho Ugen Tsechup, President of the Bhutan Football Federation (BFF), utilized the historic visit to outline ambitious upcoming initiatives. “Because of his hectic schedule, [the time] was short. But what we discussed was concise, to the point,” Ugen Tsechup explained. “With the assistance of FIFA, so much more now can be done in Bhutan.” He detailed a comprehensive development plan that includes the Rama academy and school project for men and women, commercial upgrades to existing football infrastructure at Changjiji and GMC, and the construction of a new stadium in Paro. When asked to highlight a single project from the Infantino era that he was most proud of, Ugen Tsechup declined, emphasizing the cumulative effect of consistent support. “I can’t single even one out, because every investment has been an important contribution to the development of football in Bhutan,” he said. “The headquarters, giving us independence... the academy, the infrastructure, the grounds, the mini-pitches, the futsal pitches—each and every aspect of the infrastructure development contributed by FIFA has added an important moment for the Bhutan Football Federation.” This localized investment is having a profound human impact, particularly in the women's game. Pema Choden Tshering, Captain of the Bhutan Women’s National Team, has witnessed the transformation of the sport's baseline firsthand. “I grew up playing in dusty fields. I now get to play on artificial turf, on grass fields as well, through my international match experiences,” Tshering noted. She pointed to the establishment of a girls’ academy in Gelephu—where over 60 girls receive regular, year-round training—as a direct result of improved infrastructure. Tshering also credited the FIFA Forward programme for funding vital match experiences that allow the squad to test themselves internationally. “That has provided a lot of opportunity for the girls to grow, not just as players, but also as a person,” she added. With national team players now securing international contracts, Tshering is optimistic: “I hope this will inspire our future girls as well, and also encourage our parents to allow more girls to play the sport.” While elite European football traditionally dominates the media landscape, the administrative reality for countries like Mauritania, Bangladesh, and Bhutan is that consistent, structured investment is creating a new baseline. By marrying reliable funding with clear talent pathways and grassroots infrastructure, FIFA is establishing the necessary foundation for the global game to grow equitably.

item.title: Kulusevski admits he feared long-term injury could end his career
item.description: Kulusevski admits he feared long-term injury could end his career Dejan Kulusevski admitted that he told people close to him that he might not return to football because of his long-term knee injury. The Swede had not featured for Spurs in 526 days before he was brought on as a substitute in their 3-1 win over Coventry at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. In a clash with Marc Guehi, Kulusevski suffered a knee injury that would keep him out not just Spurs’ Europa League final win, but for a whole season. During that time period, he missed the reigns of two permanent managers, Igor Tudor and Thomas Frank. The winger received a standing ovation from the Spurs crowd when he came onto the pitch and played a part in helping Spurs over the line in their first Premier League win since they beat Everton 1-0 on the final day of last season. “The journey felt impossible. It was the most difficult it could be, but I had a feeling I was going to come back to play football. I just had to believe and that is what I do,” he explained after the match. “I had to tell my closest ones it might not work out, just a couple of months ago, but in my heart I always knew it would work out. “I kept working, 10 hours every day when no one is watching, so when everything was impossible and everyone gave up, I never gave up because of this that happened today. “God gives me all the power. I can’t take credit for what I have done because I haven’t done it alone. Every day he has been doing it for me.” Roberto De Zerbi said after the match that he brought Kulusevski on “for the fans” who have “suffered” over the last two years with back-to-back 17th-place finishes in the Premier League. “I am so grateful that they miss me play,” the Swede said about the fans reception for him. “It means a lot and I am here to show them a better me. And a better me will be a better Spurs so we will be good.” “I was not nervous. I was ready to play. It was fun, it was fun.” “I will tell everyone about the journey. It has been an amazing journey even if it is hard sometimes. Hard is beautiful and I am so grateful that I had to experience it. “Now I am ready to play football. I see myself a little differently now. I think I am a different man now. Same guy, same guy who wants to play football but a little bit smarter.”

item.title: Are Yankees making right move keeping Aaron Boone? Scouts, exec have strong (and mixed) opinions
item.description: The Yankees have considered changing managers since being swept out of the postseason by the World Series-bound Rays two weeks ago. How could they not? Managing general partner Hal Steinbrenner and general manager Brian Cashman couldn’t ignore all those former Yankees calling out the organization for bad clubhouse culture. Those big names included Derek Jeter, Alex Rodriguez, CC Sabathia, Paul O’Neill, Joe Girardi and Anthony Rizzo. As NJ.com has been predicting , the Yankees will be sticking with Aaron Boone , although Monday night’s reports were slightly premature. NJ.com baseball columnist Bob Klapisch reported Tuesday that a final decision will be made soon for Boone to manage the final year of his contract, which will be his 10 th since succeeding Girardi. Klapisch also reported that this is Steinbrenner’s call and the upcoming work stoppage has played a role in the decision to retain Boone. If the Yankees fired Boone now and found a replacement in a few weeks, the new manager wouldn’t be permitted to talk to his players from the time the lockout begins on Dec. 1 until it ends. The offseason is a critical bonding period for new managers and players. If this lockout lasts until summer, as many predict, spring training could be shortened to three weeks instead of six, similar to 2020 when COVID shortened the season to 60 games. Boone’s time with the Yankees is checkered. He has a great regular-season résumé — nine consecutive winning seasons, eight postseasons, one pennant and a .583 winning percentage that is second among active managers and 17 th best all-time. But Boone hasn’t won a World Series, and it’s now been 17 years since the Yankees’ last championship in 2009. Also, clubhouse culture criticism reflects poorly on any skipper. Are Jazz Chisholm’s antics on Boone? Does Cashman deserve blame for trading for a player who was a problem with the Marlins? Are the Yankees making the right move in keeping Boone? NJ.com sought opinions from four people in baseball who follow the Yankees closely. All four were granted anonymity because they’re not authorized by their organizations to publicly comment on opposing teams. Here’s their take: NATIONAL LEAGUE SCOUT “I like Aaron Boone. I think that his inability to have the courage to sit Jazz Chisholm when he needed to sit became a problem. I saw Joe Torre lose the clubhouse when he was in New York, Charlie Manuel lose the clubhouse when he was in Philly. I saw Terry Francona lose the clubhouse when he was in Boston. I’m seeing the same thing with Aaron. That doesn’t make them bad managers, but sometimes you need a change. Sometimes you need somebody that’s not so nice to the players. “When you watch the Yankees, you see all the lackadaisical crap, the bonehead defensive plays, the bonehead baserunning, the Jazz Chisholm show. That’s sadly a young, five-tool player who hurts you more than he’ll ever help you. “I would have made a change. I think Aaron’s a good manager. He’s a good person. He sticks

That’s sadly a young, five-tool player who hurts you more than he’ll ever help you. “I would have made a change. I think Aaron’s a good manager. He’s a good person. He sticks up for his players. He takes the slings for some of the crap his players do, but at a certain point, you can’t just continue to be their friend. “Pat Murphy just took the Brewers to the World Series. He benches guys, but you never hear anyone say, “I wouldn’t want to play for Murphy.’ His guys love him because it’s consistent. If Aaron Judge pissed Pat Murphy off, Pat Murphy would call out Aaron Judge. I don’t think Aaron Boone would do that. Even when Murphy was the Brewers’ bench guy, if guys were screwing around during a spring training practice, he’d air them out in front of whoever was there. I don’t think Aaron Boone would ever do that. “Yeah, I think the Yankees need a change. There are good managers out there who would air guys out. Buck Showalter isn’t young, but he wouldn’t be a bad choice. Brandon Hyde wouldn’t be a bad choice.” AMERICAN LEAGUE SCOUT 1 “You know what? That’s a tough one. I’d keep Boone there. I like what he’s done. It ain’t his fault that a pitcher can’t win a big game. It’s not his fault that Aaron Judge gets hurt. It’s not his fault that Giancarlo Stanton is overpaid and can’t stay on the field. And it’s not Boone’s fault that Cashman doesn’t move some of those minor leaguers or players to go out get pieces to help them win. That’s why Judge is chirping now. “The stuff that Jazz is getting away with, that is on Boone, and that’s when he needs to clamp down. I know it’s New York, and I know Boone would get hollered at by management for being too tough, but at some point, you’ve got to sit Jazz down for a week and prove a point. Sometimes you have to do that. Sometimes you’ve got to call a guy out like that. Then you go to the people above you and say, ‘Look, if you want to win and you want to get the best of this guy, you got to call him out.’ Jazz knows he can get away with it and he knows Boone ain’t gonna call him out, so nothing’s gonna be done, and I think that’s total BS. “Here’s another thing: Teams used to be afraid of the Yankees. Not anymore. They’re on even ground now. Baltimore is not afraid of them anymore. Toronto’s not afraid of them anymore. Tampa definitely’s not afraid of them. The Yankees have more stars and a bigger payroll, but other teams now say, ‘Be patient, boys, something stupid is going to happen. Let’s wait to see what Jazz does.’ That’s on the whole organization. That’s on Boone. That’s on Cashman. That’s on Steinbrenner. Yeah.” NATIONAL LEAGUE EXECUTIVE “I guess the first thing is, who are you going to go get to replace Boone if the Yankees fired him? You’ve got teams out there right now that can’t find a manager. Look at some of the teams that hired guys in the last year. Who’s better than Boone? Now I’m not saying Boone’s the greatest, but who do you want to put on the list? That would be my question to all the people that want to replace him. “I think it’s going to be a short year next year. It’s the last year of Boone’s contract. Give him one more shot. Get everybody healthy. If everybody was healthy this year, they might win the division. You never know. “The bottom line, I don’t think the Yankees are outmanaged. At the end of the day, these guys have to hit the ball, play the game, field the ball. Right? They obviously pitched well. It again came down to the playoffs where they were a couple hits away here and there. I didn’t see a team that was outmanaged, but the culture is definitely something that you could address as being a real thing. “Culture is a very big deal. I would say that there were some issues this year. Obviously, you see a guy with a sucker in his mouth out in the field. That’s a problem. But I don’t know if it was just Jazz. “I don’t know that the culture was bad. It might be a little stale at some point. On every team, eventually things run stale. Was Dusty Baker a bad manager? He moved around four or five times to different teams and the guy should be or will be a Hall of Fame manager. He was great for culture. “I wonder if Boone has anyone policing the clubhouse. In Boston, the Red Sox always had Dustin Pedroia and David Ortiz to police Manny Ramirez. Was anyone there to do that on the Yankees this year? Judge was hurt half the year and not on every roadtrip. Giancarlo Stanton wasn’t around almost the whole year. I don’t know. “Again, when I watched the Yankees, I didn’t see a team that was getting outmanaged and I’ll come back to who are you getting that’s better than Boone? I can’t think of anyone.” AMERICAN LEAGUE SCOUT 2 “I don’t think Boone’s the problem. I don’t think Boone’s ever been allowed to manage. I think Boone’s given a script, and he follows the script. There’s a reason why Joe Girardi was let go. He didn’t follow the script. It’s a symptom of Major League Baseball now. Stuff comes down from the front office, the manager is giving a script and he runs with it. When Cashman says Boone is making the lineup, I have zero belief in that. Zero. “I think Boone’s biggest flaw is he hasn

item.title: NFL in Paris: League eyes big debut as Steelers-Saints game comes amid security concerns
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) aims a pass during the second half of an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Tampa, Fla., Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026. (AP Photo/Chris O'Meara) Chris O'Meara The NFL hopes to bring a “mini-Super Bowl” vibe to Paris this week for its first regular-season game in France, even as authorities consider imposing curfews following civil unrest . The security situation has partially overshadowed the buildup to Sunday’s game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at Stade de France. But the league says preparations are on schedule with an “NFL House” to open later in the week and other fan activities. The Saints arrived in Paris on Monday morning and have their own fan events planned, too. The NFL has teamed up with Paris Saint-Germain and French stars like Kylian Mbappé and rugby player Antoine Dupont to help promote the game. Brett Gosper, the NFL’s head of Europe and Asia-Pacific, told The Associated Press that the French market has been one of “high interest” for some time. “It would make sense to play regularly here each year, but we haven’t made that call yet,” Gosper said in a recent interview. “We like to see how things go the first time, but we’re pretty confident it will be a successful execution of that game.” To land lucrative media-rights deals in any market, the league knows it needs to attract new fans and push higher into that country’s TV viewership preferences. “(The) Super Bowl is your first meeting, normally, with new entrants, so if we can make this week as much like a Super Bowl as possible, a mini–Super Bowl, then we’ll hopefully recruit some new fans this week and that’s the whole goal,” Gosper said. NFL: ‘No disruption’ The league said Sunday that “preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France.” “We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters,” the NFL’s statement read. ”We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There’s been no disruption or impact at league sites.” The Saints left for Paris from New York shortly after beating the Giants 34-27 on Sunday. “Our guys are really looking forward to this. It’s going to be an awesome setup, awesome opportunity,” coach Kellen Moore said at his postgame news conference. Mbappé, PSG part of the plan Soccer club PSG announced it has partnered with the NFL on two distinct game jerseys. Saints players were also invited to PSG’s Champions League game against Barcelona at Parc des Princes on Tuesday night. Mbappé, the France and Real Madrid star, pulls on shoulder pads and a helmet in an NFL social media segment with Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson . “It works very well and it raises the profile and it makes the game more accessible to people who aren’t as familiar with it in that country,” Gosper said of the collaborations. item.content:encoded: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) aims a pass during the second half of an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Tampa, Fla., Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026. (AP Photo/Chris O'Meara) Chris O'Meara The NFL hopes to bring a “mini-Super Bowl” vibe to Paris this week for its first regular-season game in France, even as authorities consider imposing curfews following civil unrest . The security situation has partially overshadowed the buildup to Sunday’s game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at Stade de France. But the league says preparations are on schedule with an “NFL House” to open later in the week and other fan activities. The Saints arrived in Paris on Monday morning and have their own fan events planned, too. The NFL has teamed up with Paris Saint-Germain and French stars like Kylian Mbappé and rugby player Antoine Dupont to help promote the game. Brett Gosper, the NFL’s head of Europe and Asia-Pacific, told The Associated Press that the French market has been one of “high interest” for some time. “It would make sense to play regularly here each year, but we haven’t made that call yet,” Gosper said in a recent interview. “We like to see how things go the first time, but we’re pretty confident it will be a successful execution of that game.” To land lucrative media-rights deals in any market, the league knows it needs to attract new fans and push higher into that country’s TV viewership preferences. “(The) Super Bowl is your first meeting, normally, with new entrants, so if we can make this week as much like a Super Bowl as possible, a mini–Super Bowl, then we’ll hopefully recruit some new fans this week and that’s the whole goal,” Gosper said. NFL: ‘No disruption’ The league said Sunday that “preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France.” “We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters,” the NFL’s statement read. ”We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There’s been no disruption or impact at league sites.” The Saints left for Paris from New York shortly after beating the Giants 34-27 on Sunday. “Our guys are really looking forward to this. It’s going to be an awesome setup, awesome opportunity,” coach Kellen Moore said at his postgame news conference. Mbappé, PSG part of the plan Soccer club PSG announced it has partnered with the NFL on two distinct game jerseys. Saints players were also invited to PSG’s Champions League game against Barcelona at Parc des Princes on Tuesday night. Mbappé, the France and Real Madrid star, pulls on shoulder pads and a helmet in an NFL social media segment with Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson . “It works very well and it raises the profile and it makes the game more accessible to people who aren’t as familiar with it in that country,” Gosper said of the collaborations. Antoine Griezmann, a former France international soccer star who now plays for Orlando City in Major League Soccer, has been a big NFL supporter through the years through podcasts and TV appearances. Rugby plays a role Another gateway into the French sports scene is through rugby, Gosper said, speaking before last weekend. “This is a very strong sports market. Yes, it’s dominated by soccer, but rugby has a big part in it,” said Gosper, the former CEO of World Rugby. “The familiarity with a physical sport like rugby, we think helps, as it has in the UK and Australia. People are used to watching collisions and contact and enjoy that and like to see a different version of that. So, we think that’s helpful in France.” France rugby star Antoine Dupont will be at Sunday’s game. He once spent a day at the training facility of the Los Angeles Chargers and showed coach Jim Harbaugh how to pass a rugby ball. The Americans are coming Just what France needs: more Americans. “There’s a particularly high U.S. inbound on this,” Gosper said, estimating around 20%, which is higher than a typical London game. The stadium capacity is about 82,000. He said 70% of the tickets were bought locally, and the remaining 10% are from elsewhere in Europe. “We don’t announce sellouts, but the stadium is full,” Gosper said. Climbing the ladder State-owned France Televisions is covering Sunday’s game. “They’re seeing this as a major national event in France. They’ll have a very big free-to-air audience,” Gosper said. Sports daily L’Equipe also will have a free-to-air broadcast, and its print edition recently published an NFL supplement for readers. “You want to rise up that viewing preference ladder on French broadcasts over time. We know if we get into that top five it starts paying back,” Gosper said. “You do that by increasing the number of fans, engaging really well with them, being part of the local landscape, and that happens over time.” Download the FREE WPXI News app for breaking news alerts. item.title: Erik ten Hag accuses Cristiano Ronaldo of ‘letting down’ Manchester United
item.description: Ten Hag says Ronaldo did not complete post-match run Former manager claims club broke promises made to him Erik ten Hag has claimed Cristiano Ronaldo “let the team down” during their time together at Manchester United. Ten Hag has also alleged that promises made by United’s owners went unfulfilled, leading to his sacking by the club in October 2024 . Ronaldo returned for a second spell at United in August 2021 and was already at the club when Ten Hag was appointed in April 2022 as Ole Gunnar Solskjær’s successor . The relationship between the pair quickly broke down, however, with Ronaldo refusing to come on as a substitute in a win against Tottenham in October 2022 before he then publicly criticised the club in a TV interview . The forward’s contract was mutually terminated the following month. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Villarreal’s Iñigo Pérez ready to meet Iraola again in test of old bond
item.description: Refused a work permit at Bournemouth, Pérez comes face to face with Liverpool’s head coach in Champions League On Iñigo Pérez’s first day as a head coach he took a call from Andoni Iraola, just as he had every day for months. They had known each other for 22 years, lived in the same residency, come through the same academy and played in the same team; they had worked side by side, manager and assistant, and embarked on an adventure together. Now, though, Pérez was having to go it alone. At 36, he had become what his friend thought he would be from the moment they met, just not so soon. “He wished me luck and said he was there for me,” Pérez said, “said that if I ever needed anything …” Well, maybe not anything . Continue reading...

item.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Sid Lowe
item.content:encoded: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Leaving England is scary but I’m here to win’: Charlie Cresswell on Ligue 1 life and his international dream
item.description: Young centre-back could not see a way forward at Leeds so moved to France. Now he’s preparing for the biggest game of his life against Juventus By Get French Football News “Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision,” says Charlie Cresswell. It is a decision that he never thought he would make. His father, Richard, made a career as a footballer in England; his brother, Alfie, was coming through Leeds’s academy; Charlie was on the fringes of the Leeds first team when the opportunity to join Toulouse arose in 2024. “That was the biggest decision I made in football,” he says. “I’ve been a Leeds fan since I was eight. I’d been at the club since I was 10, but, looking back, I was 20 years old with no games and I needed to get out and go play,” says Cresswell, now at Rennes and preparing to face Juventus in the Europa League. Continue reading...

item.title: Konsa bullish about Arsenal’s Champions League hopes as Bayern clash looms
item.description: Centre-back has settled right in at Arsenal and is looking ‘to win everything’, starting with Wednesday’s duel against Harry Kane For Ezri Konsa, it was just a wonderfully satisfying challenge. The Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap had stolen in behind him up the inside left channel on Sunday. There were 93 minutes gone, Arsenal were 1-0 up and it was now or never for Forest. Konsa decreed that it would be never, curving his covering run back, matching Delap for pace and stretching into the perfect block tackle. So, another win for Arsenal : their 10th in 11 matches this season. Another clean sheet. And for Konsa, a continuation of what has been a dreamlike couple of months. Do points-saving last-minute challenges mean more when the defender is actually a fan of the club, too? Basically, yes. Continue reading...

item.title: Semenyo’s eight-week injury absence leaves Manchester City short on cover for Haaland
item.description: Ghana forward sustained knee injury against Ipswich Maresca to ring changes against AEK Athens on Tuesday Antoine Semenyo has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury, leaving Enzo Maresca short of alternatives to Erling Haaland, who is a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League game at home against AEK Athens on Tuesday. Semenyo limped off against Ipswich on Saturday and Haaland hobbled off at full time with a foot injury. City are eager to get their European campaign back on track after losing against Paris Saint-Germain last Wednesday. Maresca has said he will make changes and has admitted previously that Haaland will require resting at some point. Semenyo would have been the most obvious replacement but Phil Foden and Iliman Ndiaye could be utilised. Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern‑day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win against Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago. Continue reading...
